//! Aggregate consumers may choose a seek order; ordinary pages keep their order.
use super::{catalog::{Catalog, TableInfo}, intent, intent_walk};
use crate::ast::{ArgDecl, Expr, FunctionBody, FunctionDecl, Literal, ReadExpr};
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};

// @ref LLP 3000.013#5.1 — choose an access path, leaving aggregate scan
// admission and streaming to the consumer's existing binder/runtime contract.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub(super) struct Contexts {
    pub domains: BTreeSet<String>,
    pub extrema: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    required: BTreeMap<String, BTreeSet<String>>,
}
impl Contexts {
    pub fn safe(&self, read: &ReadExpr, value: &Expr) -> bool {
        safe_endpoint(value, self.required.get(&read.site.to_string()).unwrap_or(&BTreeSet::new()))
    }
    fn visit(&mut self, value: &mut Expr, tables: &BTreeMap<String, TableInfo>, functions: &BTreeMap<String, FunctionDecl>, required: &BTreeSet<String>) {
        if let Expr::Read(read) | Expr::Exists { read, .. } = value {
            self.required.insert(read.site.to_string(), required.clone());
        }
        if let Expr::Call { name, args, .. } = value
            && is_consumer(name, args, tables) && !functions.contains_key(name)
            && let Some(Expr::Read(read)) = args.first() && read.range.is_none() {
            self.domains.insert(read.site.to_string());
            if matches!(name.as_str(), "min" | "max") && let Some(field) = args.get(1).and_then(intent::column) {
                self.extrema.insert(read.site.to_string(), field.into());
            }
        }
        consumer(value, tables, functions, required);
    }
}
pub(super) fn order(catalog: &mut Catalog) -> Contexts {
    let mut contexts = Contexts::default();
    for doc in &mut catalog.documents {
        for program in &mut doc.programs {
            let required = required_args(&program.args);
            let mut visit = |value: &mut Expr| contexts.visit(value, &catalog.tables, &catalog.functions, &required);
            intent_walk::statements(&mut program.prelude, &mut visit);
            intent_walk::statements(&mut program.body, &mut visit);
        }
        for function in &mut doc.functions {
            let required = required_args(&function.args);
            let mut visit = |value: &mut Expr| contexts.visit(value, &catalog.tables, &catalog.functions, &required);
            match &mut function.body {
                FunctionBody::Expression(value) => intent_walk::expression(value, &mut visit),
                FunctionBody::Block(body) => intent_walk::statements(body, &mut visit),
            }
        }
        for shape in &mut doc.shapes {
            intent_walk::shape(&mut shape.fields, &mut |value| contexts.visit(value, &catalog.tables, &catalog.functions, &BTreeSet::new()));
        }
    }
    contexts
}

// @ref LLP 3000.019#3.2 — defer overload selection to the typed binder.
// Optional filters and inferred lanes may materialize an ordinary read before
// then. Keep the unpaged domain as an alternative for a scalar projection;
// a binary collection comparison still receives its original page plan.
pub(super) fn remember_domains(catalog: &mut Catalog) {
    for doc in &mut catalog.documents {
        intent_walk::document(doc, &mut |expr| {
            if let Expr::Call { name, args, .. } = expr
                && matches!(name.as_str(), "min" | "max") && args.len() == 2
                && !catalog.functions.contains_key(name) && intent::column(&args[1]).is_none()
                && let Expr::Read(read) = &args[0]
                && read.range.is_none() && read.matching.is_none()
                && catalog.tables.get(&read.table).is_some_and(|table|
                    !table.maintained.as_ref().is_some_and(|maintain| maintain.by.is_empty())) {
                catalog.extremum_domains.insert(read.site.to_string(), read.clone());
            }
        });
    }
}

fn required_args(args: &[ArgDecl]) -> BTreeSet<String> {
    args.iter().filter(|arg| !arg.type_.optional).map(|arg| arg.name.clone()).collect()
}

pub(super) fn is_consumer(name: &str, args: &[Expr], tables: &BTreeMap<String, TableInfo>) -> bool {
    if matches!(name, "count" | "sum") { return true; }
    if !matches!(name, "min" | "max") { return false; }
    let field = args.get(1).and_then(intent::column);
    // @ref LLP 3000.019#3.2 — expression extrema use ordinary aggregate scan planning.
    // Collection-valued second arguments keep binary page comparison planning.
    if field.is_none() && args.get(1).is_none_or(may_be_collection) { return false; }
    // A binary comparison of two pages keeps their observable row order.
    // A focal member absent from this table can belong to an outer shape.
    match args.first() {
        Some(Expr::Read(read)) => tables.get(&read.table).is_some_and(|table|
            extremum_domain(read, table) && field.is_none_or(|field| field == "id" || table.columns.contains_key(field))),
        _ => true,
    }
}

// Before type binding, only select an aggregate order for a definitely scalar
// result. Otherwise leave the source order intact for the binary overload;
// the binder can still admit a scalar aggregate over that ordinary scan.
fn may_be_collection(value: &Expr) -> bool {
    match value {
        Expr::Literal { .. } | Expr::Unary { .. } | Expr::Exists { .. } | Expr::Created { .. } => false,
        Expr::Binary { op, left, right, .. } if op == "??" || op == "+" => may_be_collection(left) || may_be_collection(right),
        Expr::Binary { .. } => false,
        Expr::If { then, otherwise, .. } => may_be_collection(then) || may_be_collection(otherwise),
        Expr::Assert { value, .. } => may_be_collection(value),
        // Calls can be user helpers, including helpers which return pages.
        _ => true,
    }
}

fn extremum_domain(read: &ReadExpr, table: &TableInfo) -> bool {
    if !read.order_keys.is_empty() || read.range.is_some() || read.matching.is_some()
        || read.filter.is_some() || !read.seeks.is_empty() || read.keys.is_empty() { return true; }
    // Decide the argument's kind before adding an aggregate order. In
    // particular, a complete maintained group lookup is a scalar total.
    // Positional keys without an index retain their point/refusal path;
    // only the binder can resolve their types or diagnose an ambiguity.
    let named = read.keys.iter().all(|key| key.column.is_some());
    if !named && read.index.is_none() { return false; }
    let index = read.index.as_deref().or_else(|| table.maintained.as_ref().map(|_| "byGroup"));
    !table.indexes.iter().any(|candidate| candidate.unique && candidate.is_plain()
        && index.is_none_or(|name| candidate.name == name)
        && (candidate.columns.len() == read.keys.len()
            || named && table.total_unique(candidate) && candidate.columns.len() < read.keys.len())
        && (!named || candidate.columns.iter().all(|column| read.keys.iter().any(|key| key.column.as_ref() == Some(column)))))
}

fn consumer(value: &mut Expr, tables: &BTreeMap<String, TableInfo>, functions: &BTreeMap<String, FunctionDecl>, required: &BTreeSet<String>) {
    match value {
        Expr::Call { name, args, .. } if is_consumer(name, args, tables) && !functions.contains_key(name) => {
            choose_consumer(name, args, tables, required);
        }
        Expr::Exists { read, .. } => choose(read, tables, required),
        _ => {},
    }
}

pub(super) fn choose_consumer(name: &str, args: &mut [Expr], tables: &BTreeMap<String, TableInfo>, required: &BTreeSet<String>) {
    if !is_consumer(name, args, tables) { return; }
    let field = if matches!(name, "min" | "max") { args.get(1).and_then(intent::column).map(str::to_owned) } else { None };
    let Some(Expr::Read(read)) = args.first_mut() else { return; };
    if let Some(field) = field
        && read.index.is_none() && read.order_keys.is_empty() && read.range.is_none() && read.matching.is_none()
        && let Some(table) = tables.get(&read.table) {
        let mut conjuncts = Vec::new();
        if let Some(filter) = &read.filter { intent::split(*filter.clone(), &mut conjuncts); }
        let mut pins = read.keys.iter().filter_map(|key| key.column.clone()).collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
        pins.extend(conjuncts.iter().filter_map(|value| intent::equality(value, table).map(|(column, _)| column)));
        let pins: Vec<_> = pins.into_iter().collect();
        if !pins.iter().any(|pin| pin == "id") && table.indexes.iter().any(|index| index.is_plain()
            && index.columns.get(pins.len()) == Some(&field) && index.columns[..pins.len()].iter().all(|column| pins.contains(column))) {
            read.order_keys.push(field);
            return;
        }
    }
    choose(read, tables, required);
}

pub(super) fn choose(read: &mut ReadExpr, tables: &BTreeMap<String, TableInfo>, required: &BTreeSet<String>) {
    // A page bound makes row order observable even inside count/sum. Explicit
    // authored order/index choices also retain their existing meaning.
    if read.index.is_some() || !read.order_keys.is_empty() || read.range.is_some() || read.matching.is_some() { return; }
    let Some(table) = tables.get(&read.table) else { return; };
    let mut conjuncts = Vec::new();
    if let Some(filter) = &read.filter { intent::split(*filter.clone(), &mut conjuncts); }
    let mut pins = read.keys.iter().filter_map(|key| key.column.clone()).collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
    pins.extend(conjuncts.iter().filter_map(|value| intent::equality(value, table).map(|(column, _)| column)));
    // A pinned intrinsic id already bounds the read to one row. Inserting an
    // order column after this prefix would create the invalid (id, col, id).
    if pins.contains("id") { return; }
    let mut ranges = BTreeMap::<String, (bool, bool)>::new();
    let mut unsafe_columns = BTreeSet::new();
    for (column, op, endpoint) in conjuncts.iter().filter_map(intent::comparison)
        .chain(read.seeks.iter().map(|seek| (seek.column.clone(), seek.op.clone(), seek.value.clone()))) {
        if pins.contains(&column) { continue; }
        if !safe_endpoint(&endpoint, required) { unsafe_columns.insert(column); continue; }
        let bound = ranges.entry(column).or_default();
        bound.0 |= op.starts_with('>');
        bound.1 |= op.starts_with('<');
    }
    // Choosing the order makes ordinary planning extract both endpoints. A
    // safe sibling must not hoist another bound out of its short-circuit guard.
    ranges.retain(|column, _| !unsafe_columns.contains(column));
    // Prefer a two-sided window, then a canonical column name. Permuting
    // conjunctions must not churn an automatically chosen index identity.
    let column = ranges.iter().find(|(_, (lower, upper))| *lower && *upper).or_else(|| ranges.first_key_value());
    if let Some((column, _)) = column { read.order_keys.push(column.clone()); }
}

pub(super) fn safe_endpoint(value: &Expr, required: &BTreeSet<String>) -> bool {
    // These values are present before any row predicate runs. Parameters
    // cannot be reassigned or shadowed. Numeric interval proofs admit only
    // arithmetic that stays within the safe-integer range for every input.
    match value {
        Expr::Literal { value, .. } => !matches!(value, Literal::Null),
        Expr::Name { name, .. } => matches!(name.as_str(), "now" | "viewer") || required.contains(name),
        Expr::Unary { .. } | Expr::Binary { .. } => numeric_interval(value, required).is_some(),
        _ => false,
    }
}


fn numeric_interval(value: &Expr, required: &BTreeSet<String>) -> Option<(i128, i128)> {
    let max = i128::from(snapback4_core::value::I53_MAX);
    let (low, high) = match value {
        Expr::Literal { value: Literal::Number(number), .. } => { let n = number.parse().ok()?; (n, n) }
        Expr::Name { .. } if safe_endpoint(value, required) => (-max, max),
        Expr::Unary { op, value, .. } if op == "-" => { let (lo, hi) = numeric_interval(value, required)?; (-hi, -lo) }
        Expr::Binary { op, left, right, .. } => {
            let (a, b) = numeric_interval(left, required)?;
            let (c, d) = numeric_interval(right, required)?;
            match op.as_str() {
                "+" => (a + c, b + d),
                "-" => (a - d, b - c),
                "*" => { let products = [a * c, a * d, b * c, b * d]; (*products.iter().min()?, *products.iter().max()?) }
                _ => return None,
            }
        }
        _ => return None,
    };
    (low >= -max && high <= max).then_some((low, high))
}

//! Binder-only expression ownership. No grouping enters the executed IR.
use super::*;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum Owner { Condition, Payload }
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub(crate) struct Owned { pub kind: Owner, pub by: String }
pub(crate) type Ownership = BTreeMap<String, Owned>;

// @ref LLP 3000.007#19.1 — ownership travels beside flat baseline statements, never through their lowering or serialization.
#[derive(Default)]
pub(super) struct Body {
    pub code: Vec<Stmt>,
    pub ownership: Ownership,
}

impl std::ops::Deref for Body {
    type Target = [Stmt];
    fn deref(&self) -> &[Stmt] { &self.code }
}

impl Body {
    pub fn push(&mut self, stmt: Stmt) { self.code.push(stmt); }

    pub fn nest(&mut self, prefix: &str, ownership: &Ownership) {
        self.ownership.extend(ownership.iter().map(|(path, owner)| (format!("{prefix}.{path}"), Owned { kind: owner.kind, by: format!("{prefix}.{}", owner.by) })));
    }

    pub fn extend(&mut self, other: Body) {
        let offset = self.len();
        self.ownership.extend(other.ownership.into_iter().map(|(path, owner)| {
            (shift(&path, offset), Owned { kind: owner.kind, by: shift(&owner.by, offset) })
        }));
        self.code.extend(other.code);
    }

    pub fn push_if(&mut self, condition: Expr, then_body: Body, else_body: Body) {
        self.nest(&format!("{}.then", self.len()), &then_body.ownership);
        self.nest(&format!("{}.else", self.len()), &else_body.ownership);
        self.push(Stmt::If { condition, then_body: then_body.code, else_body: else_body.code });
    }

    pub fn push_for(&mut self, binding: String, domain: LoopDomain, body: Body) {
        self.nest(&format!("{}.loop", self.len()), &body.ownership);
        self.push(Stmt::For { binding, domain, body: body.code });
    }

    pub fn own(&mut self, start: usize, owner: Owner) {
        // More deeply nested owners remain: an emit's setup resets effect
        // control even when that emit occurs in another condition's helper.
        let by = self.len().to_string();
        for index in start..self.len() {
            let entry = self.ownership.entry(index.to_string()).or_insert_with(|| Owned { kind: owner, by: by.clone() });
            if owner == Owner::Payload { *entry = Owned { kind: owner, by: by.clone() }; }
        }
    }
}

/// Translate only the side map through baseline helper-return lowering.
/// No branch here can change the code that helper_returns receives or emits.
/// Original statement ownership includes a new guard around that statement;
/// nested ownership follows it into :then. A return's two assignments share
/// its ownership, and a loop's generated break has no expression owner.
pub(super) fn helper_ownership(body: &Body) -> Ownership {
    if body.ownership.is_empty() { return Ownership::new(); }
    let mut paths = BTreeMap::new();
    helper_paths(&body.code, "", "", &mut paths);
    let mut result = Ownership::new();
    for (path, owner) in &body.ownership {
        for target in &paths[path].cover {
            result.insert(target.clone(), Owned { kind: owner.kind, by: paths[&owner.by].statement.clone() });
        }
    }
    result
}

fn shift(path: &str, offset: usize) -> String {
    let (head, tail) = path.split_once('.').map_or((path, String::new()), |(head, tail)| (head, format!(".{tail}")));
    format!("{}{tail}", head.parse::<usize>().unwrap() + offset)
}

struct Location { cover: Vec<String>, statement: String }

fn child(prefix: &str, index: usize) -> String {
    if prefix.is_empty() { index.to_string() } else { format!("{prefix}.{index}") }
}

fn helper_paths(body: &[Stmt], source: &str, target: &str, paths: &mut BTreeMap<String, Location>) -> bool {
    let mut may_return = false;
    let mut offset = 0;
    for (index, stmt) in body.iter().enumerate() {
        let from = child(source, index);
        let to = child(target, offset);
        let inner = if may_return { format!("{to}.then.0") } else { to.clone() };
        let returns = match stmt {
            Stmt::Return(_) => true,
            Stmt::If { then_body, else_body, .. } => {
                let a = helper_paths(then_body, &format!("{from}.then"), &format!("{inner}.then"), paths);
                let b = helper_paths(else_body, &format!("{from}.else"), &format!("{inner}.else"), paths);
                a || b
            }
            Stmt::For { body, .. } => helper_paths(body, &format!("{from}.loop"), &format!("{inner}.loop"), paths),
            // Write-condition setup does not contain helper-local returns;
            // baseline helper_returns leaves it alone.
            Stmt::WriteTarget { condition: Some(condition), .. } => {
                unchanged_paths(&condition.setup, &format!("{from}.condition"), &format!("{inner}.condition"), paths);
                false
            }
            _ => false,
        };
        let width = if !may_return && matches!(stmt, Stmt::Return(_)) { 2 } else { 1 };
        paths.insert(from, Location { cover: (0..width).map(|n| child(target, offset + n)).collect(), statement: inner });
        offset += width;
        may_return |= returns;
    }
    may_return
}

fn unchanged_paths(body: &[Stmt], source: &str, target: &str, paths: &mut BTreeMap<String, Location>) {
    for (index, stmt) in body.iter().enumerate() {
        let from = child(source, index);
        let to = child(target, index);
        paths.insert(from.clone(), Location { cover: vec![to.clone()], statement: to.clone() });
        match stmt {
            Stmt::If { then_body, else_body, .. } => {
                unchanged_paths(then_body, &format!("{from}.then"), &format!("{to}.then"), paths);
                unchanged_paths(else_body, &format!("{from}.else"), &format!("{to}.else"), paths);
            }
            Stmt::For { body, .. } => unchanged_paths(body, &format!("{from}.loop"), &format!("{to}.loop"), paths),
            Stmt::WriteTarget { condition: Some(condition), .. } => unchanged_paths(&condition.setup, &format!("{from}.condition"), &format!("{to}.condition"), paths),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
}

pub(crate) fn runtime_path(program: &str, path: &str) -> String {
    let mut result = program.to_owned();
    for part in path.split('.') {
        match part { "loop" => {}, "then" | "else" | "condition" => { result.push(':'); result.push_str(part); }, index => {
            let Ok(index) = index.parse::<usize>() else { return String::new(); };
            result.push_str(&format!(":{}", index + 1));
        } }
    }
    result
}

// @ref LLP 3000.036.001#17 — parent-pinned pages use stored snapshot keys.

pub(crate) fn lower_program(program: &mut ProgramDecl, fields: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeSet<String>>) {
    if program.kind != ProgramKind::Query || program.native || !program.prelude.is_empty() { return; }
    body(&mut program.body, fields, &BTreeMap::new(), &mut 0);
}

fn body(statements: &mut Vec<Stmt>, fields: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeSet<String>>, inherited: &BTreeMap<String,String>, serial: &mut usize) {
    let mut rows = inherited.clone();
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for mut stmt in std::mem::take(statements) {
    if let Stmt::Bind { value, .. } | Stmt::Return { value, .. } = &mut stmt {
                let read = match value { Expr::Read(read) => Some(read), Expr::Shape { base, .. } | Expr::ShapeUse { base, .. } =>
                    if let Expr::Read(read) = base.as_mut() { Some(read) } else { None }, _ => None };

                    let mut selected = BTreeMap::new();

                        let Expr::Member { base, name, site } = value else { return };
                        let Expr::Name { name: row, .. } = base.as_ref() else { return };
                        if !rows.get(row).and_then(|table| fields.get(table)).is_some_and(|fields| fields.contains(name)) { return; }
                        let key = (row.clone(),name.clone());
                        let site = site.clone();
                        let snapshot = value.clone();
                        let fixed = selected.entry(key).or_insert_with(|| {
                            *serial += 1; let fixed = format!("$pageKey{serial}");
                            out.push(Stmt::Bind { names: vec![fixed.clone()], value: snapshot, site: site.clone() }); fixed
                        }).clone();
                        *value=Expr::Name {name:fixed,site:site.clone()};
                    });
                }
            }
        match &mut stmt {
            Stmt::Bind { names, value, .. } => {
                for name in names.iter() { rows.remove(name); }
                let [name] = names.as_slice() else { out.push(stmt); continue };
                if let Expr::Assert { value, .. } = value && let Expr::Read(read) = value.as_ref()
                    && !read.keys.is_empty() && read.range.is_none() && read.filter.is_none() && read.matching.is_none()
                    && fields.contains_key(&read.table) { rows.insert(name.clone(),read.table.clone()); }

//! Capture bare searches, then admit optional indexes against their bound plans.
//! The authored device program never acquires a membership predicate.
use super::catalog::Catalog;
use crate::ast::*;

// @ref LLP 3000.007#18.1 — a plain unique search order lowers to the same
// scoped words index as column order, before needle/browse variants diverge.
pub(super) fn named_order(table: &super::catalog::TableInfo, read: &mut ReadExpr) -> bool {
    if read.matching.is_none() || !read.order_keys.is_empty()
        || super::validate_key_names(read).is_err() { return false; }
    let Some(index) = table.indexes.iter().find(|index| Some(&index.name) == read.index.as_ref()) else { return false; };
    if !index.unique || !index.is_plain() || read.keys.len() > index.columns.len() { return false; }
    // Preserve the declared prefix contract, including positional arguments.
    // A named key outside that prefix must still be refused by the binder.
    if read.keys.iter().any(|key| key.column.as_ref().is_some_and(|column| !index.columns[..read.keys.len()].contains(column))) { return false; }
    let mut pinned: std::collections::BTreeSet<_> = read.keys.iter().enumerate()
        .map(|(n, key)| key.column.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| index.columns[n].clone())).collect();
    let mut predicates = Vec::new();
    if let Some(filter) = &read.filter { super::intent::split(*filter.clone(), &mut predicates); }
    for predicate in predicates {
        if let Some((column, _)) = super::intent::equality(&predicate, table) { pinned.insert(column); }
    }
    read.order_keys = index.columns.iter().filter(|column| !pinned.contains(*column)).cloned().collect();
    if read.order_keys.is_empty() { read.order_keys.push("id".into()); }
    for (key, column) in read.keys.iter_mut().zip(&index.columns) { key.column.get_or_insert_with(|| column.clone()); }
    // Keep the authored choice until the alternatives are planned: a compatible
    // browse branch must not become ambiguous with an equivalent plain index.
    true
}

// @ref LLP 3000.028#3.3 — only a single bare ordinary search is inferred.
pub(super) fn capture(catalog: &mut Catalog) {
    for doc in &catalog.documents {
        for program in &doc.programs {
            if program.kind != ProgramKind::Query || program.held || !program.prelude.is_empty() { continue; }
            let [Stmt::Return { value, .. }] = program.body.as_slice() else { continue };
            let value = match value { Expr::Shape { base, .. } | Expr::ShapeUse { base, .. } => base.as_ref(), value => value };
            let Expr::Read(read) = value else { continue };
            // Column order also identifies normalized named unique reads. An
            // explicit words index without column order still stays out.
            if read.matching.is_none() || !read.keys.is_empty()
                || read.range.is_none() || read.order_keys.is_empty()
                || read.filter.as_deref().is_some_and(|value| !scalar(value)) { continue; }
            let Some(table) = catalog.tables.get(&read.table) else { continue };
            if table.maintained.is_some() { continue; }
            let Some(rule) = table.decl.rules.iter().find(|r| r.effect == Effect::Read) else { continue };
            let Expr::Exists { read: probe, .. } = &rule.value else { continue };
            let Some(members) = catalog.tables.get(&probe.table) else { continue };
            if members.decl.expire.is_some() || members.maintained.is_some() { continue; }
            let module = std::path::Path::new(&doc.file).file_stem().unwrap().to_string_lossy();
            catalog.ordinary_searches.push(super::operation_name(&module, &program.name));
        }
    }
}

// @ref LLP 3000.028#3.3 — optional indexes must neither reject a baseline
// program nor change its IR. Admit only after the bound audience and portable
// key/label checks succeed; a declined candidate leaves no schema cost.
pub(super) fn provision(catalog: &mut Catalog, schema: &mut snapback4_core::schema::Schema, programs: &[super::BoundProgram]) {
    use snapback4_core::{ir, schema::{IndexComponent, RuleExpr, RuleTerm}, search_plan::ordinary};
    for bound in programs {
        if !catalog.ordinary_searches.contains(&bound.program.name) { continue; }
        let Some(scan) = ir::scans(&bound.program).into_iter().find(|scan|
            matches!(scan.prefix.last(), Some(ir::IndexKeyExpr::WordPrefix(_)))) else { continue };
        let table = schema.tables[&scan.table].clone();
        let RuleExpr::Exists { table: members, index: point, key, .. } = &table.rules.read else { continue };
        let [RuleTerm::Field(scope), RuleTerm::Viewer] = key.as_slice() else { continue };
        let mut index = table.indexes[&scan.index].clone();
        // Prefix exactly the bound ordinary index. Its equality pins, word
        // position and full cursor ordering suffix must survive unchanged.
        index.components.insert(0, IndexComponent::Column(scope.clone()));
        let existing_words = table.indexes.iter().find(|(_, old)| old.components == index.components).map(|(name, _)| name.clone());
        let info = &catalog.tables[&scan.table];
        let Some(mut declaration) = info.indexes.iter().find(|i| i.name == scan.index).cloned() else { continue };
        declaration.columns.insert(0, scope.clone());
        let Some((position, _)) = &mut declaration.words else { continue };
        *position += 1;
        declaration.site = bound.site.clone();
        let new_words = existing_words.is_none();
        declaration.name = existing_words.unwrap_or_else(|| super::intent::index_name(info, &declaration));
        let mut candidate = schema.clone();
        candidate.tables.get_mut(&scan.table).unwrap().indexes.insert(declaration.name.clone(), index.clone());
        // Online-only memberships do not get sync's reverse audience index.
        // Provision it in the same speculative candidate as the target words
        // index; neither is retained when admission or portable bounds fail.
        let source_info = &catalog.tables[members];
        let source_table = &schema.tables[members];
        let columns = source_table.index(point).map(|index| index.columns()).unwrap_or_default();
        let [parent, principal] = columns.as_slice() else { continue };
        let source_columns = vec![principal.clone(), parent.clone(), "id".into()];
        let source_decl = if source_table.indexes.values().any(|index| index.is_plain() && index.columns().starts_with(&source_columns[..2])) { None }
            else {
                let Some(mut source) = source_info.indexes.iter().find(|index| index.is_plain()).cloned() else { continue };
                source.columns = source_columns.clone(); source.unique = false; source.words = None;
                source.site = bound.site.clone(); source.name = super::intent::index_name(source_info, &source);
                candidate.tables.get_mut(members).unwrap().indexes.insert(source.name.clone(), snapback4_core::schema::Index {
                    components: source_columns.into_iter().map(IndexComponent::Column).collect(), unique: false,
                });
                Some(source)
            };
        if ordinary::plan(&candidate, &bound.program).is_none() { continue; }
        let mut errors = Vec::new();
        super::key_bound::check(catalog, &candidate, &mut errors);
        if !errors.is_empty() || !snapback4_core::schema::validate(&candidate).is_empty() { continue; }
        if let Some(source) = source_decl {
            schema.tables.get_mut(members).unwrap().indexes.insert(source.name.clone(), candidate.tables[members].indexes[&source.name].clone());
            catalog.synthesized.insert((members.clone(), source.name.clone()));
            catalog.tables.get_mut(members).unwrap().indexes.push(source);
        }
        if new_words {
            schema.tables.get_mut(&scan.table).unwrap().indexes.insert(declaration.name.clone(), index);
            catalog.synthesized.insert((scan.table.clone(), declaration.name.clone()));
            catalog.tables.get_mut(&scan.table).unwrap().indexes.push(declaration);
        }
    }
}

fn scalar(value: &Expr) -> bool {
    match value {
        Expr::Literal { .. } | Expr::Name { .. } => true,
        Expr::Member { base, .. } => matches!(base.as_ref(), Expr::Focal { .. }),
        Expr::Unary { value, .. } => scalar(value),
        Expr::Binary { left, right, .. } => scalar(left) && scalar(right),
        _ => false,
    }
}

//! Immutable release custody: digest the required tree and flush it before DB selection.
// @ref LLP 3000.000.000#5-hot-activation-and-ownership — source durability precedes the database's release pointer.
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
use std::{
    fs,
    io::{Read, Write},
    path::{Path, PathBuf},
};

fn files(root: &Path, path: &Path, out: &mut Vec<PathBuf>) -> Result<(), String> {
    let mut entries = fs::read_dir(path)
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
        .map(|e| e.map(|e| e.path()).map_err(|e| e.to_string()))
        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
    entries.sort();
    for path in entries {
        let relative = path.strip_prefix(root).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        if relative
            .components()
            .next()
            .is_some_and(|c| c.as_os_str() == ".snapback4")
        {
            continue;
        }
        let m = fs::symlink_metadata(&path).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        if m.is_dir() {
            files(root, &path, out)?;
        } else if m.is_file() {
            out.push(path);
        } else {
            return Err(format!(
                "immutable release artifact must be a real directory or regular file: {}",
                path.display()
            ));
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}
pub(crate) fn digest(root: &Path) -> Result<String, String> {
    let mut paths = Vec::new();
    files(root, root, &mut paths)?;
    let mut hash = Sha256::new();
    for path in paths {
        let name = path.strip_prefix(root).unwrap().to_string_lossy();
        // @ref LLP 3000.000.000.000.000#4-cli-surface-contracts — metadata does not change executable release identity.
        if name == ".pending-adoption" || name == "provenance.json" {continue;}
        hash.update((name.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
        hash.update(name.as_bytes());
        #[cfg(unix)]
        use std::os::unix::fs::OpenOptionsExt;
        let mut options = fs::OpenOptions::new();
        options.read(true);
        #[cfg(unix)]
        options.custom_flags(libc::O_NOFOLLOW);
        let mut file = options.open(&path).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        hash.update(
            file.metadata()
                .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
                .len()
                .to_le_bytes(),
        );
        let mut buffer = [0u8; 16384];
        loop {
            let n = file.read(&mut buffer).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
            if n == 0 {
                break;
            }
            hash.update(&buffer[..n]);
        }
    }
    Ok(format!("{:x}", hash.finalize()))
}
pub(crate) fn durable(root: &Path) -> Result<(), String> {
    let mut paths = Vec::new();
    files(root, root, &mut paths)?;
    for path in paths {
        fs::File::open(path)
            .and_then(|f| f.sync_all())
            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    }
    fn dirs(path: &Path) -> Result<(), String> {
        for e in fs::read_dir(path).map_err(|e| e.to_string())? {
            let e = e.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
            if e.file_type().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?.is_dir() {
                dirs(&e.path())?;
            }
        }
        fs::File::open(path)
            .and_then(|f| f.sync_all())
            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())
    }
    dirs(root)
}

pub(crate) fn link_store(root: &Path) -> Result<(), String> {
    let project = crate::project::Project { root: root.into() };
    snapback4_core::private_fs::directory(&project.data_dir()).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let path = project.store_path();
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        let target = Path::new("../../../store.sqlite");
        match fs::symlink_metadata(&path) {
            Ok(m) if m.file_type().is_symlink() => {
                if fs::read_link(&path).map_err(|e| e.to_string())? != target {
                    fs::remove_file(&path).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
                    std::os::unix::fs::symlink(target, &path).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
                }
            }
            Ok(_) => {
                return Err(format!(
                    "release store path must be a symbolic link: {}",
                    path.display()
                ));
            }
            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
                std::os::unix::fs::symlink(target, &path).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
            }
            Err(e) => return Err(e.to_string()),
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    #[cfg(not(unix))]
    Err("serving shared releases requires Unix symbolic links".into())
}

pub(crate) struct Pointer {
    staged: PathBuf,
    dir: PathBuf,
    release: u64,
    previous: Option<u64>,
    rollback: bool,
    ledger: fs::File,
}
impl Pointer {
    pub(crate) fn prepare(
        dir: &Path,
        release: u64,
        previous: Option<u64>,
        rollback: bool,
    ) -> Result<Self, String> {
        let pointer = dir.join("current");
        if pointer.exists() && !pointer.is_file() {
            return Err("current must be a regular release pointer file".into());
        }
        let staged = dir.join(format!(".current-{}-{release}", std::process::id()));
        let file = snapback4_core::private_fs::file(&staged, true).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        let mut prepared = Self {
            staged,
            dir: dir.into(),
            release,
            previous,
            rollback,
            ledger: file,
        };
        writeln!(prepared.ledger, "{release}")
            .and_then(|_| prepared.ledger.sync_all())
            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        prepared.ledger = fs::OpenOptions::new()
            .create(true)
            .append(true)
            .open(dir.join("releases.jsonl"))
            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        writeln!(prepared.ledger,"{}",serde_json::json!({"at":snapback4_core::now_ms(),"release":release,"previous":previous,"rollback":rollback,"state":"prepared"})).and_then(|_|prepared.ledger.sync_all()).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
        Ok(prepared)
    }
    pub(crate) fn finish(&mut self, generation: u64) -> Result<(), String> {
        fs::rename(&self.staged,self.dir.join("current")).and_then(|_|fs::File::open(&self.dir)?.sync_all()).map_err(|e|format!("release {} committed in database, but current copy failed: {e}; inspect `snapback4 releases {}`",self.release,self.dir.display()))?;
        writeln!(self.ledger,"{}",serde_json::json!({"at":snapback4_core::now_ms(),"release":self.release,"previous":self.previous,"rollback":self.rollback,"generation":generation,"state":"activated"})).and_then(|_|self.ledger.sync_all()).map_err(|e|format!("release committed, but ledger completion failed: {e}"))
    }
}
impl Drop for Pointer {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if self.staged.exists() {
            let _ = fs::remove_file(&self.staged);
        }
    }
}

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000#16-release-reactivation-and-rollback-foresight-rel5 — deletion requires a definitive non-commit, never a lost reply.
pub(crate) struct Candidate { dir: PathBuf, release: u64, pub committed: bool }
impl Candidate {
    pub(crate) fn new(dir: &Path, release: u64) -> Self { Self {dir:dir.into(),release,committed:false} }
}
impl Drop for Candidate {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if self.committed { return; }
        let probe=(|| -> Result<bool,String> {
            let store=snapback4_core::Store::open_read_only(&self.dir.join("store.sqlite")).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
            let history:bool=store.conn().query_row("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_schema WHERE type='table' AND name='_release_events')",[],|r|r.get(0)).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
            if !history {return Ok(false);}
            store.conn().query_row("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _release_events WHERE release=?1 OR previous=?1)",[self.release as i64],|r|r.get(0)).map_err(|e|e.to_string())
        })();
        match probe {
            Ok(false)=>if let Err(e)=fs::remove_dir_all(self.dir.join("releases").join(self.release.to_string())) {eprintln!("uncommitted release {} cleanup failed: {e}",self.release);},
            Ok(true)=>{},
            Err(e)=>eprintln!("release {} outcome unknown; retained source for recovery; inspect releases: {e}",self.release),
        }
    }
}

//! Actions share argument types and API names with mutations, with no data-plane body.
use super::{BoundProgram, catalog::Catalog, operation_name};
use crate::ast::{Expr as A, Literal, ScalarType, TypeKind, WorkDecl};
use crate::diag::{Diagnostic, Fallible, Site, type_error, unknown};
use crate::types::{Ty, scalar_to_arg};
use snapback4_core::ir::{BinaryOp, Expr, Input, Program, ProgramKind, Stmt, UnaryOp};
use snapback4_core::value::Value;
use snapback4_core::schema::{ActionSpec, Schema, WorkSpec};
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};

pub(super) fn bind(catalog: &Catalog, schema: &mut Schema, programs: &mut Vec<BoundProgram>, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
    for doc in &catalog.documents {
        let module = std::path::Path::new(&doc.file).file_stem().and_then(|s| s.to_str()).unwrap_or("schema");
        for decl in &doc.actions {
            let name = operation_name(module, &decl.name);
            let root = if module == "schema" { &decl.name } else { module };
            if programs.iter().any(|p| p.program.name == name || (p.program.kind != ProgramKind::Job && (p.module != "schema") != (module != "schema") && if p.module == "schema" { p.program.name == root } else { p.module == root })) {
                diagnostics.push(unknown(&decl.site, format!("duplicate operation or API module {name}"), "rename the action or its module"));
                continue;
            }
            let result = (|| -> Fallible<(BoundProgram, ActionSpec)> {
                let mut args = BTreeMap::new();
                let mut types = Vec::new();
                for arg in &decl.args {
                    if args.contains_key(&arg.name) {
                        return Err(unknown(&arg.site, format!("duplicate argument {}", arg.name), "rename one argument"));
                    }
                    validate_type(&arg.type_, catalog, &arg.site, false)?;
                    args.insert(arg.name.clone(), scalar_to_arg(&arg.type_));
                    types.push((arg.name.clone(), Ty::from_scalar(&arg.type_)));
                }
                let mut result_type = Ty::Unknown;
                let returns = if let Some(fields) = &decl.returns {
                    let mut returns = BTreeMap::new();
                    let mut types = BTreeMap::new();
                    for field in fields {
                        if returns.contains_key(&field.name) {
                            return Err(unknown(&field.site, format!("duplicate result field {}", field.name), "declare each result field once").guide("actions"));
                        }
                        validate_type(&field.type_, catalog, &field.site, true)?;
                        returns.insert(field.name.clone(), scalar_to_arg(&field.type_));
                        types.insert(field.name.clone(), Ty::from_scalar(&field.type_));
                    }
                    result_type = Ty::Object(types);
                    Some(returns)
                } else { None };
                let spec = ActionSpec { returns, work: bind_work(&decl.work, &decl.site)? };
                let condition = rule(&decl.rule)?;
                // Admission is the only IR body: it cannot read, write or emit.
                let body = vec![Stmt::Require { condition, code: "E_RULE".into(), site: Some(format!("actions.{name}")), message: None }];
                Ok((BoundProgram { maintenance_scopes: Default::default(), statement_ends: Vec::new(), page_sources: Default::default(), canonical_sources: Default::default(), constraint_domains: Default::default(), filters: Default::default(), view_types: Default::default(), sources: Default::default(), receipt_sources: Vec::new(), receipt_returns: Vec::new(), implicit_write_results: Vec::new(), selections: Default::default(), timeline_scans: Default::default(), program: Program { name, kind: ProgramKind::Action, args, read_time_granularity_ms: None, body, native: false, returned_shapes: Default::default() }, presence: None, module: module.into(), args: types, result: result_type, notes: Vec::new(), site: decl.site.clone(), job_bound_helpers: Default::default() }, spec))
            })();
            match result {
                Ok((program, spec)) => {
                    schema.action_specs.insert(program.program.name.clone(), spec);
                    programs.push(program);
                }
                Err(error) => diagnostics.push(error),
            }
        }
    }
}

// @ref LLP 3000.009#5.1 — result refs are IDs, and only declared bounded fields can settle.
fn validate_type(ty: &ScalarType, catalog: &Catalog, site: &Site, result: bool) -> Fallible<()> {
    let bad = |message| type_error(site, message, "use a bounded scalar type or list of scalars; references name declared tables").guide("actions");
    match &ty.kind {
        TypeKind::Cursor if result => return Err(bad("an action result cannot contain a query cursor")),
        TypeKind::Text { min, max, .. } if *max == 0 || min.is_some_and(|min| min > *max) => return Err(bad("text needs a positive maximum at least as large as its minimum")),
        TypeKind::Json { max } | TypeKind::Bytes { max } | TypeKind::Image { max, .. } | TypeKind::Video { max } | TypeKind::File { max, .. } if *max == 0 => return Err(bad("a bounded type needs a positive maximum")),
        TypeKind::Ref { table } if !catalog.tables.contains_key(table) => return Err(bad("an action type references an unknown table")),
        TypeKind::List { item, max, .. } => {
            if *max == 0 { return Err(bad("a list needs a positive maximum")); }
            validate_type(item, catalog, site, result)?;
        }
        TypeKind::Enum { variants } => {
            let unique: BTreeSet<_> = variants.iter().collect();
            if unique.len() != variants.len() { return Err(bad("enum variants must be distinct")); }
        }
        _ => {}
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub(super) fn bind_work(decl: &WorkDecl, site: &Site) -> Fallible<WorkSpec> {
    let mut work = WorkSpec::default();
    let mut secrets = BTreeSet::new();
    for secret in &decl.secrets {
        let valid = secret.bytes().next().is_some_and(|b| b.is_ascii_uppercase() || b == b'_')
            && secret.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_uppercase() || b.is_ascii_digit() || b == b'_');
        let reserved = ["SNAPBACK_", "SNAPBACK4_", "NODE_", "DYLD_", "LD_", "LC_"].iter().any(|prefix| secret.starts_with(prefix))
            || matches!(secret.as_str(), "PATH" | "HOME" | "TMPDIR" | "TMP" | "TEMP" | "LANG" | "TZ" | "SHELL" | "ENV" | "BASH_ENV" | "IFS" | "PWD" | "USER" | "LOGNAME");
        if !valid || reserved {
            return Err(type_error(site, format!("secret {secret} must be an uppercase environment name outside the runtime's reserved names"), "secrets [MAIL_API_KEY]").guide("actions"));
        }
        if !secrets.insert(secret.clone()) {
            return Err(unknown(site, format!("duplicate secret {secret}"), "declare each secret once").guide("actions"));
        }
    }
    work.secrets = secrets.into_iter().collect();
    if let Some(value) = decl.max_attempts { work.policy.max_attempts = value; }
    if let Some(value) = decl.backoff_ms { work.policy.backoff_ms = value; }
    work.policy.deadline_ms = decl.deadline_ms;
    if let Some(value) = decl.cancellable { work.policy.cancellable = value; }
    if !work.policy.valid() {
        return Err(type_error(site, "work policy requires retry 1–100 total attempts, backoff 1s–5m, and deadline 1s–30d", "retry 8 backoff 2s deadline 1h cancellation allow").guide("actions"));
    }
    Ok(work)
}

fn rule(expr: &A) -> Fallible<Expr> {
    Ok(match expr {
        A::Name { name, .. } if matches!(name.as_str(), "allow" | "deny") => Expr::Literal(Value::Bool(name == "allow")),
        A::Unary { op, value, .. } if op == "not" => Expr::Unary { op: UnaryOp::Not, value: Box::new(rule(value)?) },
        A::Binary { op, left, right, .. } if op == "and" || op == "or" => Expr::Binary { op: if op == "and" { BinaryOp::And } else { BinaryOp::Or }, left: Box::new(rule(left)?), right: Box::new(rule(right)?) },
        A::Binary { op, left, right, .. } if op == "=" || op == "!=" => {
            let principal = |e: &A| match e { A::Literal { value: Literal::Str(s), .. } if snapback4_core::value::identity_fits(s) && s != snapback4_core::SYSTEM_PRINCIPAL => Some(s.clone()), _ => None };
            let viewer = |e: &A| matches!(e, A::Name { name, .. } if name == "viewer");
            let value = if viewer(left) { principal(right) } else if viewer(right) { principal(left) } else { None };
            let Some(value) = value else { return Err(bad_rule(expr)); };
            Expr::Binary { op: if op == "=" { BinaryOp::Eq } else { BinaryOp::Ne }, left: Box::new(Expr::Input(Input::Viewer)), right: Box::new(Expr::Literal(Value::Id(value))) }
        }
        _ => return Err(bad_rule(expr)),
    })
}

fn bad_rule(expr: &A) -> Diagnostic {
    type_error(expr.site(), "an action rule compares viewer with a principal; it cannot read data or arguments", "action invite(email: text <=200) <- viewer = 'service:worker'  -- or allow / deny").guide("actions")
}

+  finally {rmSync(path,{force:true});}
+  return {status:'passed',cases:['reactivation','refused-deploy-cleanliness','rollback-foresight','old-client-diff','installed-v1-v2-guide']};
+}

//! The client's types, by inference: one generated TypeScript module with
//! the row types, every operation's argument and result types, and the
//! `api` object the app imports. Built, never committed.

pub mod lean;
pub mod rust;
pub use rust::rust;
mod server;
mod receipts;
mod settlement;
mod compat;
pub use server::server_typescript;

use crate::bind::{Bound, BoundProgram};
use crate::types::Ty;
use snapback4_core::ir::ProgramKind;
use snapback4_core::schema::{ColumnType, Schema};
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

pub fn typescript(bound: &Bound) -> String { typescript_inner(bound, None) }

/// A complete saved schema is the explicit compatibility baseline; release is an author label.
pub fn typescript_spanning(bound: &Bound, baseline: &Bound, since: u64) -> String {
    typescript_inner(bound, Some((baseline, since)))
}

fn typescript_inner(bound: &Bound, compatibility: Option<(&Bound, u64)>) -> String {
    let baseline = compatibility.map(|(bound, _)| bound);
    let since = compatibility.map(|(_, release)| release);
    let mut out = String::new();
    out.push_str("// Generated by snapback4 from snapback/*.q. Do not edit; edit the schema.\n");
    out.push_str("// Mutation predicts is per operation: eligible may render a pending row before useMutation().run() settles; never has no predicted row.\n// Eligibility needs a device and held facts; otherwise the write queues. run() waits for sent/failed unless waitSeconds: 0 requests custody.\n// UI proofs await a fresh sent receipt before asserting committed data; a rendered pending row is not a commit.\n");
    let action = if bound.server { "Action, " } else { "" };
    let ephemeral = if bound.schema.operations.values().any(|f| f.ephemeral) { "Ephemeral, " } else { "" };
    let following = if bound.schema.timelines.is_empty() { "" } else { "FollowingQuery, " };
    let receipts = if bound.schema.receipts.is_empty() { "" } else { "ReceiptFamily, " };
    out.push_str(&format!("import type {{ {action}Cursor, {ephemeral}Mutation, {receipts}{following}Query }} from \"snapback4/contract\";\n\n"));
    // @ref LLP 3000.000.000.000#3-generated-compatibility — generated modules have no package runtime dependency.
    out.push_str(include_str!("emit/availability.ts"));
    out.push_str("export type Rows = {\n");
    for (name, table) in bound.schema.visible_tables() {
        out.push_str(&format!("  {}: {{\n", property(name)));
        for (column, kind) in table.columns.iter().filter(|(name, _)| name.as_str() != "$global" && !table.engine_field(name) && !snapback4_core::schema::timeline::is_slot(name)) {
            // @ref LLP 3000.040#15-generated-typescript — a bound is documented, not branded: the server's E_INPUT is the guarantee.
            if column_has_int_range(kind) { out.push_str(&format!("    /** {kind} */\n")); }
            let mut scales = Vec::new();
            scale_docs(&Ty::from_column(kind), column, &mut scales);
            if !scales.is_empty() { out.push_str(&format!("    /** {} */\n", scales.join("; "))); }
            let before = baseline.and_then(|b| b.schema.table(name)).and_then(|t| t.columns.get(column));
            let added = baseline.and_then(|b| b.schema.table(name)).is_some() && before.is_none();
            if added { out.push_str(&format!("    /** Since release {}; optional: releases before {} lack this column. */\n", since.unwrap(), since.unwrap())); }
            let ty = before.map(|old| compat::result(&Ty::from_column(kind), Some(&Ty::from_column(old)), since)).unwrap_or_else(|| column_ts(kind, &bound.schema));
            out.push_str(&format!("    {}{}: {};\n", property(column), if table.private_field(column) || baseline.and_then(|b| b.schema.table(name)).is_some_and(|t| t.private_field(column)) || added { "?" } else { "" }, ty));
        }
        out.push_str("    /** True on this device's own unconfirmed change (the card). */\n    pending?: boolean;\n");
        if table.through.is_some() && table.sync.is_some() && table.leave == snapback4_core::schema::LeavePolicy::DeliveredHistory {
            out.push_str("    /** Delivered history, outside the current parent page. */\n    retained?: boolean;\n");
        }
        out.push_str("  };\n");
    }
    let views = &bound.view_types;
    for (name, ty) in views { out.push_str(&format!("  {}: {};\n", property(name), compat::result(ty, baseline.and_then(|b| b.view_types.get(name)), since))); }
    out.push_str("};\n\n");
    if bound.schema.visible_tables().any(|(_,table)| !table.maintained.is_empty()) {
        out.push_str("export type WriteRows = {\n");

            for (name, ty) in &program.args { scale_docs(ty, name, &mut scales); }

            let bounds = program.program.args.iter().filter(|(_, ty)| has_list_minimum(ty))
                .map(|(name, ty)| format!("{name}: {}", arg_bound(ty)))
                .collect::<Vec<_>>();
            if !bounds.is_empty() { comment.push_str(&format!(" Bounds: {}.", bounds.join("; "))); }
            if fact.held { comment.push_str(" Held: device only; server refuses E_QUERY_HELD; no server fallback."); }
            if program.program.kind == ProgramKind::Query {
                comment.push_str(" Read.cut: meter | words | null, beside complete. Unwrap with isReady(read) && read.data, or matchRead(read, handlers) from snapback4/contract (also snapback4/react).");
                // Which React hook takes this query: `usePage` needs a cursor argument named `c`.
                let paged = program.args.iter().any(|(name, ty)| name == "c" && ty_ts(ty).starts_with("Cursor"));
                comment.push_str(if kind == "FollowingQuery" { HOOK_FOLLOWING } else if paged { HOOK_PAGE } else { HOOK_QUERY });
            }
            if fact.connected_effects_only { comment.push_str(&format!(" {}.", crate::bind::residency::CONNECTED_EFFECTS)); }
            if program.program.kind == ProgramKind::Mutation && !fact.ephemeral {

                } else {
                    " Timing: with a device and held facts, a pending row may render before run() settles; otherwise queues without a predicted row."
                });

            }
            out.push_str(&format!("{indent}/** {} */\n", comment.replace("*/", "* /")));

            let args = compat::args(&program.args, old.map(|p| p.args.as_slice()), since);
            let result = compat::result(&program.result, old.map(|p| &p.result), since);
            out.push_str(&format!("{indent}{}: {kind}<{args}, {result}> & {{ available(release: ReleaseSnapshot): boolean }};\n", property(short)));
        }
        if module != "schema" {
            out.push_str("  };\n");
        }
    }
    out.push_str("};\n\n");
    out.push_str(if bound.schema.receipts.is_empty() { "export const api: Ops = {\n" } else { "const operations: Ops = {\n" });
    for (module, programs) in &modules {

        if module != "schema" {
            out.push_str(&format!("  {}: {{\n", property(module)));
        }
        for program in programs {
            let short = program.program.name.rsplit('.').next().unwrap_or(&program.program.name);

                ProgramKind::Query => "query",
                ProgramKind::Mutation => "mutation",
                ProgramKind::Action => "action",
                ProgramKind::Job => continue,
            };
            let fact = &bound.schema.operations[&program.program.name];
            let words = fact.runs.as_ref().map(|word| format!(", runs: {}", string_literal(word))).or_else(|| fact.predicts.as_ref().map(|word| format!(", predicts: {}", string_literal(word)))).unwrap_or_default();
            let words = if fact.ephemeral {

            let available = format!(", available: (release) => operationAvailable(release, {}, \"{kind}\", {args})", string_literal(&program.program.name));
            out.push_str(&format!("{indent}{}: {{ kind: \"{kind}\", name: {}{words}{available} }},\n", property(short), string_literal(&program.program.name)));
        }
        if module != "schema" {
            out.push_str("  },\n");
        }
    }
    out.push_str("};\n");
    receipts::emit(bound, &mut out);
    out
}

//! The server opt-in is an authoring boundary, never a schema or wire flag.
use crate::ast::Document;
use crate::diag::{Diagnostic, Site};
use std::collections::BTreeSet;

// @ref LLP 3000.009.000#1 — only actions, routes and action schedules require the opt-in; effects and service seats stay core.
pub(super) fn admit(documents: &mut [Document], diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
    // Like identity, a directive in any loaded module applies project-wide.
    if documents.iter().any(|doc| doc.server) { return; }
    let actions: BTreeSet<_> = documents.iter().flat_map(|doc| {
        let module = std::path::Path::new(&doc.file).file_stem().and_then(|s| s.to_str()).unwrap_or("schema");
        doc.actions.iter().map(move |decl| super::operation_name(module, &decl.name))
    }).collect();
    let mut refuse = |site: &Site, form: String, guide: &str| {
        diagnostics.push(Diagnostic::new(site, "E_SERVER_REQUIRED",
            format!("{form} requires use server; add it once in any module (schema.q is usual) to enable the whole project; repeating it is harmless. The directive gates actions, routes and schedules naming an action. Effects (including secrets, retry, backoff, deadline and cancellation), jobs, schedules naming a job and service seats need no directive."), "use server").guide(guide));
    };
    for doc in documents {
        for decl in doc.actions.drain(..) { refuse(&decl.site, format!("action {}", decl.name), "actions"); }
        for decl in doc.routes.drain(..) { refuse(&decl.site, format!("route {}", decl.name), "routes"); }
        doc.schedules.retain(|decl| {
            if !actions.contains(&decl.target) { return true; }
            refuse(&decl.site, format!("schedule {} targeting action {}", decl.name, decl.target), "actions");
            false
        });
    }
}

//! File-qualified helper calls lower to the same global declaration before
//! planner/provenance analysis. Qualification never creates a second helper.
use crate::{ast::*, diag::Diagnostic, print};
use std::{collections::BTreeMap, path::Path};

pub(super) fn normalize(documents: &mut [Document], diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
    let owners: BTreeMap<_, _> = documents.iter().flat_map(|doc| {
        let module = Path::new(&doc.file).file_stem().and_then(|s| s.to_str()).unwrap_or("schema");
        doc.functions.iter().map(move |f| (f.name.clone(), module.to_owned()))
    }).collect();
    let mut visit = |value: &mut Expr| {
        let Expr::Call { name, args, site } = value else { return; };
        // @ref LLP 3000.007#23 — aliases lower before planning; an explicitly declared helper keeps its meaning.
        if matches!(name.as_str(), "len" | "length") && !owners.contains_key(name) { *name = "count".into(); }
        let Some((module, helper)) = name.split_once('.') else { return; };
        let Some(owner) = owners.get(helper) else { return; };
        if module != owner {
            diagnostics.push(Diagnostic::new(site, "E_QUARRY_UNKNOWN",
                format!("helper {helper} is declared in {owner}.q, not {module}.q"),
                format!("{owner}.{helper}({})", args.iter().map(print::expression).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", "))).guide("programs"));
        }
        *name = helper.to_owned();
    };
    for doc in documents {
        super::intent_walk::document(doc, &mut visit);
        for view in &mut doc.views {
            for branch in &mut view.branches {
                if let Some(p) = &mut branch.predicate { super::intent_walk::expression(p, &mut visit); }
                super::intent_walk::shape(&mut branch.fields, &mut visit);
            }
        }
    }
}

//! Materialized Following: no authored graph bounds; all source audiences stay public.
mod prediction;
pub(super) use prediction::aggregate_sites;
use crate::{ast::*, diag::{Diagnostic, Fallible}};
use snapback4_core::schema::{timeline::{Timeline, HISTORY_WINDOW}, Audience, ColumnDefault, ColumnType, Horizon, RuleExpr, RuleTerm, Schema, Table};
use super::catalog::Catalog;
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};

pub fn expand(mut documents: Vec<Document>, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) -> Vec<Document> {
    let declarations: Vec<_> = documents.iter().flat_map(|doc| doc.timelines.clone()).collect();
    let mut names = BTreeMap::<String, usize>::new();
    for doc in &documents {
        let all = doc.tables.iter().map(|v| &v.name).chain(doc.maintains.iter().map(|v| &v.name))
            .chain(doc.programs.iter().map(|v| &v.name)).chain(doc.functions.iter().map(|v| &v.name))
            .chain(doc.schedules.iter().map(|v| &v.name)).chain(doc.timelines.iter().map(|v| &v.name))
            .chain(doc.views.iter().map(|v| &v.name))
            .chain(doc.effects.iter().map(|v| &v.name)).chain(doc.shapes.iter().map(|v| &v.name))
            .chain(doc.actions.iter().map(|v| &v.name)).chain(doc.routes.iter().map(|v| &v.name));
        for name in all { *names.entry(name.clone()).or_default() += 1; }
    }
    let mut accepted = BTreeSet::new();
    for decl in &declarations {
        let owned: BTreeSet<_> = snapback4_core::schema::timeline::OWNED_SUFFIXES.iter().map(|s| format!("{}{s}", decl.name)).collect();
        let nested = declarations.iter().any(|other| other.name != decl.name && snapback4_core::schema::timeline::OWNED_SUFFIXES.iter().any(|s| format!("{}{s}", other.name) == decl.name));
        if nested || names.get(&decl.name) != Some(&1) || owned.iter().any(|n| names.contains_key(n)) {
            diagnostics.push(refusal(&decl, "E_TIMELINE_SHAPE", "timeline or owned name collides", "choose a distinct timeline name and leave its Posts, Feed, RemovedEvents, Work and Edges names unused"));
            continue;
        }
        let source = include_str!("timeline.q").replace("@T@", &decl.name);
        let (doc, errors) = crate::parse_document("timeline.q", &source);
        if !errors.is_empty() { diagnostics.extend(errors); continue; }
        for name in owned { names.insert(name, 1); }
        documents.push(doc);
        accepted.insert(decl.name.clone());
    }
    for doc in &mut documents { doc.timelines.retain(|decl| accepted.contains(&decl.name)); }
    documents
}

fn refusal(decl: &TimelineDecl, code: &str, message: impl Into<String>, rewrite: impl Into<String>) -> Diagnostic {
    Diagnostic::new(&decl.site, code, message, rewrite).guide("feeds")
}

fn owner(rule: &RuleExpr, name: &str) -> bool {
    match rule {
        RuleExpr::Eq(field, RuleTerm::Viewer) | RuleExpr::Eq(RuleTerm::Viewer, field) =>
            matches!(field, RuleTerm::Field(f) | RuleTerm::OldField(f) | RuleTerm::NextField(f) if f == name),
        RuleExpr::And(rules) => rules.iter().any(|r| owner(r, name)),
        _ => false,
    }
}

fn source<'a>(schema: &'a Schema, decl: &TimelineDecl, name: &str, actor: &str, time: Option<&str>, columns: &[(&str, ColumnType)]) -> Fallible<&'a Table> {
    let acquisition = time.map_or_else(|| "sync public, sync public last 1000, or online only".into(), |at| format!("sync public, sync public last 1000 by .{at}, or online only"));
    let fail = |message| refusal(decl, "E_TIMELINE_SHAPE", message,
        format!("declare {name} public with {acquisition}; require .{actor} = viewer for inserts and allowed deletes/updates; keep mapped fields immutable"));
    let t = schema.table(name).ok_or_else(|| fail(format!("missing timeline source {name}")))?;
    if !t.rules.read.is_public() || t.is_expiring() || schema.maintain_for(name).is_some() {
        return Err(fail(format!("{name} must be explicitly public, non-expiring application data")));
    }
    // @ref LLP 3000.016#2.1 — events have time floors; application follows admit any public residency.
    let valid_sync = match (&t.sync, time) {
        (None, _) => true,
        (Some(sync), time) if sync.audience == Audience::Public => match &sync.horizon {
            None => true,
            Some(horizon) => time.is_none_or(|at| t.index(&horizon.by)
                .is_some_and(|index| index.is_plain() && index.columns() == [at, "id"])),
        },
        _ => false,
    };
    if !valid_sync {
        return Err(fail(format!("{name} needs {acquisition}; a source floor must order by its mapped time then id")));
    }
    if !owner(&t.rules.insert, actor) || [&t.rules.update, &t.rules.delete].iter().any(|r| **r != RuleExpr::Deny && !owner(r, actor)) {
        return Err(fail(format!("{name} must retain its owner's write authority")));
    }
    for (col, ty) in columns {
        if t.columns.get(*col) != Some(ty) { return Err(fail(format!("{name}.{col} must be required {ty:?}"))); }
        if t.rules.update != RuleExpr::Deny && !t.immutable_fields().any(|f| f == *col) {
            return Err(fail(format!("{name}.{col} must be immutable")));
        }
    }
    Ok(t)
}

## 10. Wave 10 release lifecycle amendment

Commission: Charlie's REL2 workstream, 2026-10-13; implementer Codex in
sb4-w10-rel2. This amends §9.2's definition of a complete release and §2's
capture restoration. No new language, planner or device protocol is introduced.

A newly packaged numeric source directory carries `.pending-adoption`, written
and fsynced before publication. It is selectable only if database activation
history proves that its adoption committed. Successful deploy removes the marker;
a crash, refused adoption or lost control reply leaves it. `latest`, numeric
rollback, release inspection and check-release all use this rule. The database
proof recovers a committed activation even if pointer/ledger completion failed,
and recognizes its committed predecessor as proof of legacy activation.
For retained stores, committed history gates unmarked directories too, excluding
refused candidates from older binaries. Legacy stores without release history
keep their complete-source selection rule. The marker is excluded from the
source digest. All production writes of numeric
release source go through deploy; rollback and serve only select existing source.
A refused candidate remains a reserved identity and can never become a selectable
release merely because it compiles. A matching-source dormant-name refusal leads
with `rollback <dir> --to latest`; other source uses `--restore-dormant`. Human
retention evidence lists counts/samples rather than serialized inventory JSON.

Bare rollback selects the previous release of the last committed activation,
including rollback and roll-forward; prune and same-release selections are excluded. Thus v1 → v2 → v3 → v1
followed by bare rollback activates v3. An explicit --to overrides this. Legacy
stores without activation history require explicit --to. A no-op adds no event.

`deploy --check` runs the exact candidate activation on the private snapshot with
**deploy** restoration intent, while rollback/check-release previews select
restoration. No candidate is selectable and live state remains unchanged.
Preview validates static worker prerequisites without starting workers. Successful
constraint narration comes from the validated candidate after dormant projection,
not the predecessor population. Successful previews describe dormant rows/cells with counts and bounded ids,
report successful maintain rebuild source visits, and omit speculative adoption
failures and capture-fill promises. Compatibility warnings are advisory, only for
populated affected tables, and include their current row count (not a prediction
that every row is incompatible). Preview flags removed schedules and populated
removed application tables as business safeguards absent from the target. Quarry
has no hold declaration: every removed populated table gets this advisory, so a
hold's name cannot evade it. Existing live writes can change any preview result.

Retired engine capture columns retain their source table definition alongside
cells. Restoring the same read-through definition uses the preserved capture and
parent lifetime, even when the intervening release widened its read rule. The
predecessor audience correspondence barrier applies only to rows requiring new
captures. Historical rows must still pass retained reference lifetime and
capture/parent validation. A changed retained read-through definition refuses;
new rows without historical captures retain the existing first-adoption checks.
Source expiry is evaluated before projection, so restoration cannot revive an
expired captured lifetime. Recorded attribution keeps its historical value.

`run <job> --release <dir>` routes to the served store at its canonical loopback
address using `SNAPBACK4_SERVICE_TOKEN` or `--token-env NAME`; it needs no local
project/source. `POST /jobs/<job>` requires a full service capability, rechecked
under the enqueueing engine lock, and executes system work on the existing FIFO.
Every full service seat is privileged to trigger any system job; operators must
provision these tokens accordingly. Accounts, guests, read scopes and personas
are refused. `/dev/jobs` stays development-only. The reply waits for done/parked;
a lost reply is ambiguous and does not authorize automatic retry. It adds no job
priority, worker pool, token scope or idempotency contract.

`serve.lock` remains an address hint. Only successful sidecar ownership allows
reclamation. After acquiring it, an ESRCH result from kill(pid,0) identifies a dead
record and emits a diagnostic with PID, URL and directory before overwriting it.
A live/reused PID or uncertain probe never authorizes signalling or lock bypass.

Acceptance: v1/v2/rollback/refused-v3/latest and explicit refused selection;
non-numeric-history rollback; deploy preview state equality; empty/populated
warnings; all packaged rollback claims; old release E_OP/NOT_FOUND/null and exact
forward values; retained captures after widening plus deleted/reused parent and
new-row refusal; service-token job completion and unauthorized/read-only requests;
stale-lock recovery and live-owner conflict provenance. HS owns handshake/types;
DX2 owns starters/client recipes; DIAG and PAGE2 own language/planner diagnostics.


REL2 review round one: fresh GPT-6.1-sol found legacy predecessor selection,
pre-dormancy constraint narration and omitted static worker prerequisite checks.
All three were reproduced and corrected with migration, unique/narrowing and
worker-selection regressions. Review artifacts retain the verbatim findings.


REL2 round two: [Muse](./reviews/3000.000.000-rel2-wave10-r2.muse.md) and
[fresh Codex](./reviews/3000.000.000-rel2-wave10-r2.codex.md) both READY on
this amendment and implementation. Focused final verification passes. Informational
receipt sampling also covers populated items beyond empty inventory definitions;
guide consistency lives in its own test module, preserving the pre-existing
parent test file's line count. No publication or push was performed by REL2.

    39	pub(crate) fn digest(root: &Path) -> Result<String, String> {
    40	    let mut paths = Vec::new();
    41	    files(root, root, &mut paths)?;
    42	    let mut hash = Sha256::new();
    43	    for path in paths {
    44	        let name = path.strip_prefix(root).unwrap().to_string_lossy();
    45	        // @ref LLP 3000.000.000.000.000#4-cli-surface-contracts — metadata does not change executable release identity.
    46	        if name == ".pending-adoption" || name == "provenance.json" {continue;}
    47	        hash.update((name.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
    48	        hash.update(name.as_bytes());
    49	        #[cfg(unix)]
    50	        use std::os::unix::fs::OpenOptionsExt;
    51	        let mut options = fs::OpenOptions::new();
    52	        options.read(true);
    53	        #[cfg(unix)]
    54	        options.custom_flags(libc::O_NOFOLLOW);
    55	        let mut file = options.open(&path).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    56	        hash.update(
    57	            file.metadata()
    58	                .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
    59	                .len()
    60	                .to_le_bytes(),
    61	        );
    62	        let mut buffer = [0u8; 16384];
    63	        loop {
    64	            let n = file.read(&mut buffer).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    65	            if n == 0 {
    66	                break;
    67	            }
    68	            hash.update(&buffer[..n]);
    69	        }
    70	    }
    71	    Ok(format!("{:x}", hash.finalize()))
    72	}
    73	pub(crate) fn durable(root: &Path) -> Result<(), String> {
    74	    let mut paths = Vec::new();
    75	    files(root, root, &mut paths)?;
    76	    for path in paths {
    77	        fs::File::open(path)
    78	            .and_then(|f| f.sync_all())
    79	            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    80	    }
    81	    fn dirs(path: &Path) -> Result<(), String> {
    82	        for e in fs::read_dir(path).map_err(|e| e.to_string())? {
    83	            let e = e.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    84	            if e.file_type().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?.is_dir() {
    85	                dirs(&e.path())?;
    86	            }
    87	        }
    88	        fs::File::open(path)
    89	            .and_then(|f| f.sync_all())
    90	            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())
    91	    }
    92	    dirs(root)
    93	}

    95	pub(crate) fn link_store(root: &Path) -> Result<(), String> {
    96	    let project = crate::project::Project { root: root.into() };
    97	    snapback4_core::private_fs::directory(&project.data_dir()).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    98	    let path = project.store_path();
    99	    #[cfg(unix)]
   100	    {
   101	        let target = Path::new("../../../store.sqlite");
   102	        match fs::symlink_metadata(&path) {
   103	            Ok(m) if m.file_type().is_symlink() => {
   104	                if fs::read_link(&path).map_err(|e| e.to_string())? != target {
   105	                    fs::remove_file(&path).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
   106	                    std::os::unix::fs::symlink(target, &path).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
   107	                }
   108	            }
   109	            Ok(_) => {
   110	                return Err(format!(
   111	                    "release store path must be a symbolic link: {}",
   112	                    path.display()
   113	                ));
   114	            }
   115	            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
   116	                std::os::unix::fs::symlink(target, &path).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
   117	            }
   118	            Err(e) => return Err(e.to_string()),
   119	        }
   120	        Ok(())
   121	    }
   122	    #[cfg(not(unix))]
   123	    Err("serving shared releases requires Unix symbolic links".into())
   124	}

   143	            return Err("current must be a regular release pointer file".into());
   144	        }
   145	        let staged = dir.join(format!(".current-{}-{release}", std::process::id()));

   147	        let mut prepared = Self {
   148	            staged,
   149	            dir: dir.into(),
   150	            release,
   151	            previous,
   152	            rollback,
   153	            ledger: file,
   154	        };
   155	        writeln!(prepared.ledger, "{release}")
   156	            .and_then(|_| prepared.ledger.sync_all())
   157	            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
   158	        prepared.ledger = fs::OpenOptions::new()

   160	            .append(true)
   161	            .open(dir.join("releases.jsonl"))
   162	            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
   163	        writeln!(prepared.ledger,"{}",serde_json::json!({"at":snapback4_core::now_ms(),"release":release,"previous":previous,"rollback":rollback,"state":"prepared"})).and_then(|_|prepared.ledger.sync_all()).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;

   169	    }
   170	}

     6	/// Conservative input-domain inclusion: every value accepted by old is accepted by new.
     7	pub fn accepts(old: &A, new: &A) -> bool {

    10	        (A::Optional(a),A::Optional(b))=>accepts(a,b),
    11	        (A::Optional(_),_)=>false,
    12	        (a,A::Optional(b))=>accepts(a,b),
    13	        (A::Text{min:a,max:b,format:af},A::Text{min:c,max:d,format:bf})=>c<=a && d>=b && (bf.is_none() || af==bf),
    14	        (A::IntRange{..},A::Int)=>true,
    15	        (A::IntRange{min:a,max:b},A::IntRange{min:c,max:d})=>c<=a && d>=b,
    16	        (A::Enum{variants:a},A::Enum{variants:b})=>a.iter().all(|v|b.contains(v)),
    17	        (A::Bytes{max:a},A::Bytes{max:b}) | (A::Image{max:a},A::Image{max:b}) |
    18	        (A::Video{max:a},A::Video{max:b})=>b>=a,
    19	        (A::Json{max_bytes:a},A::Json{max_bytes:b})=>b>=a,

    62	/// Reports are advisory: compatibility cannot license calls or prove unchanged behavior.
    63	pub fn compare(old: &Bound, new: &Bound, label: &str) -> Vec<String> {

    70	        };
    71	        if before.program.kind!=after.program.kind {lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: operation kind changed; retain the old endpoint kind"));continue;}
    72	        for (arg,kind) in &after.program.args {
    73	            if !before.program.args.contains_key(arg) && !matches!(kind,A::Optional(_)) {
    74	                lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: clients calling without new required argument {arg} get E_INPUT; give {arg} a fitting `default <literal>` or retain a compatible wrapper"));
    75	            }
    76	        }
    77	        for (arg,kind) in &before.program.args {
    78	            match after.program.args.get(arg) {
    79	                None=>lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: removed argument {arg}; old calls sending it get E_INPUT; retain `{arg}: <old type> deprecated` on a query/mutation")),
    80	                Some(next) if !accepts(kind,next)=>lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: argument {arg} retyped or narrowed ({kind:?} → {next:?}); old values may get E_INPUT; retain the old input domain or a compatible wrapper")),
    81	                _=>{}
    82	            }
    83	        }
    84	        if result(&before.result,old)!=result(&after.result,new) {lines.push(format!("{prefix}: RESULT REVIEW: result shape/value domain changed; preserve the old projection/domain or introduce a new operation before retiring old clients"));}
    85	        if refusals(before)!=refusals(after) {lines.push(format!("{prefix}: BEHAVIOR REVIEW: refusal codes/messages changed ({:?} → {:?}); verify intended denials separately from input breaks",refusals(before),refusals(after)));}
    86	    }
    87	    lines
    88	}

snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/src/guide/deploy.md:11:For a complete real-user staging script and first-admin setup, run `guide staging`. Bulk account setup is restricted to fresh `deploy --staging` stores. Generations climb on every actual switch, including rollback and forward; selecting identical execution content is a no-op. `token --service ops --release ./deployment` works while serve runs. Signups are rate-limited: create proof accounts sequentially and respect a returned retry delay. Time-gated mutations on the real clock need a bounded retry of the authored refusal (for example `NOT_OPEN`), with a deadline and short delay; never retry unrelated refusals. Development proofs can advance the clock (`guide time`).
