snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/src/guide/deploy.md:63:Optional/defaulted columns, new tables/ops, non-unique indexes and wider types are additive. Required new fields need a literal default or explicit backfill; default now/viewer cannot invent historical values. Dev check/adoption refuses incompatible values with E_ADOPT. Release type narrowing instead retains each row whose present values cannot fit. Unique/cap conflicts still refuse atomically; repair active rows, or restore through a widened non-unique bridge, repair, then reinstate constraints. Prefer expand → migrate → contract for client compatibility.
snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/src/guide/deploy.md:70:`deploy ./deployment --check` previews deploy direction and restoration intent. `bunx snapback4 check --store ./deployment/store.sqlite --release 1` also previews a selection; `bunx snapback4 releases ./deployment latest` inspects it. Forward with `bunx snapback4 rollback ./deployment --to latest`. Preview runs exact adoption on a private disk snapshot and removes it, without activating; disk/time scales with the store, and later writes can change the plan. Release is immutable source; latest is the highest successfully adopted source even after rollback. A refused deploy removes its candidate directory and private stage. An ambiguous reply preserves source until committed history resolves the outcome; inspect releases before retrying. Bare rollback selects the previously active release; rollback prints the resolved target before preview or activation. Generation is a monotone identity; releases N/latest inspects source. Source identical to the active release is a no-op; source matching a retained release reactivates its existing id with restoration and full validation. Deploy/rollback return after serve switches: `release N is current as generation G`. In-flight one-shot operations finish in their generation; no settle sleep is needed. Default adoption is one measured receipt; --verbose/--json includes phases/cache advice. N_ADOPTION_PAUSE appears above one second. A dev/older unreachable owner requires stopping that owned process before retrying; failed adoption keeps current.
snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/src/guide/deploy.md:72:Widened enum values, or short codes a loose release wrote, become dormant rows when selected types cannot hold them; compatible forward restores exact values. Reference dependents also leave the active population. Rules, counts, maintained views and reacquired sync partitions see only active rows. Point reads/updates/ deletes see absent rows; dormant ids stay reserved. Nominal reference values stay legal, as for other missing ids; require/read-through decides live-target admission. Dormant rows occupy no cap/unique slots, so older writes can require a bridge repair. Removed tables/columns/indexes also stay dormant. Fresh-source name reuse needs --restore-dormant; selecting retained source by deploy or rollback already selects restoration. The same --restore-dormant flag is accepted by both commands. Old active updates keep dormant cells; active deletion removes them. Only active referential actions run: parent deletion invalidates dormant lifetimes. Narrowed rows with invalid visible references stay dormant; whole-table/column restoration retains its E_ADOPT barrier. Prune previews counts/bytes/sample ids; `prune ./deployment --allow-destructive` permanently drops all dormant storage. No age collector or implicit pruning exists. Deploy/rollback --allow-destructive bypasses neither validation nor retention. --allow-feed-adoption permits the explicit feed launch. Inspect releases after an ambiguous reply. Details: [SERVER.md — Release lifecycle](SERVER.md#release-lifecycle).

Rollback preview identifies current safety guards/rules and read confidentiality the target loses, active table-population changes, and current → target quotas. Preserve the current domain, audience, guard or quota in a bridge release, or pause that workflow. Old source cannot supply absent product logic. snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/src/guide/deploy.md:102:Previews lead with removed guards and their refusal codes, then group query/count active-table losses, linked dormant rows and safety dependencies per change. Verify filtered/paged/per-viewer results and denominators. Literal-default backfills print `table.column ← value on N rows` in previews and cold/hot deploy receipts: interpreted historical fields, not physical writes. Preview shows old and new rule clauses and mutation `require`s side by side, preserving Boolean parentheses. A proved tightening is a note, including `require A else X` becoming `require A else X; require B else Y` when A's refusal contract is unchanged; changed codes/messages still warn. A loosening or unproved implication is a WARNING, including rollback that removes a new guard. Unchanged clauses and consulted keys, fields, rules, auth and visibility are silent. Unread column domains and forward domain widening do not unprove a probe; narrowing still gets exact dormant-value/population warnings. Changed dependencies group once: verify refusal cases. Comparison never changes admission. Missing operations/schedules, populated removed tables, changed clauses and job bodies are named separately. An unchanged job compiling differently after a dependency change gets a note. Original read-through captures restore only with the same capture definition; new uncaptured rows still need safe audience correspondence. Receipts and previews count storage by kind: `1 row, 2 cells, 0 index entries dormant`. Dormant rows cover their retained cells; standalone cell counts/samples belong only to active rows. Bytes/assets follow the same disjoint ownership. Samples are labelled and unique within each kind/path, for example `rows notes [A]; cells notes.color [B, C]`. A retained index definition represents logical entries to rebuild, not a dormant physical index. A widening note describes values later writes could use; a compatibility WARNING counts only current values the selected release cannot hold. Compatible forward has no such warning.
snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/src/guide/deploy.md:105:Save versions/v1/schema.q (and any other .q modules with their original names) outside snapback/ and create `snapback/client-compatibility.json` containing `{"baseline":"versions/v1","since_release":2}`. `check`/`dev` emit added row/result fields as optional, labelled "Since release 2", retaining older result value domains. Required operation parameters remain required; only declared optional, defaulted or deprecated arguments may be omitted. Baseline generation also warns about old-client input breaks and result/refusal changes. This is your release label, not server generation; ordinary types stay required without opt-in. Use `row.color ?? "none"` for the baseline fallback. Keep contemporary fixtures in versions/v1/fixtures/; deploy with `--schema versions/v1` and test with `--source versions/v1` (guide testing).     fn project_insert(&self, info: &TableInfo, row: Expr) -> Expr {

            Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::ProjectFields { table: info.decl.name.clone() }, args: vec![row] }

    fn write_result_type(&self, info: &TableInfo) -> Ty {

    }

    fn calendar_number(&self, value: &A, depth: u8) -> bool {
        if depth > 8 { return false; }
        match value {
            A::Call { name, .. } => matches!(name.as_str(), "day" | "hour" | "bucket"),
            A::Name { name, .. } => self.binding(name).is_some_and(|binding| binding.revision == 0 && binding.origins.len() == 1 && self.calendar_number(&binding.origins[0].1, depth + 1)),
            A::If { then, otherwise, .. } => self.calendar_number(then, depth + 1) || self.calendar_number(otherwise, depth + 1),
            _ => false,
        }
    }

    fn field_value(&mut self, field: &ObjectField, expected: &Ty, out: &mut setup::Body) -> Fallible<(Expr, Ty)> {
        if expected.required() == Ty::Time && field.value.as_ref().map_or_else(
            || self.calendar_number(&A::Name { name: field.name.clone(), site: field.site.clone() }, 0), |value| self.calendar_number(value, 0)) {
            return Err(type_error(&field.site, "day/hour/bucket returns a period number, not a time in milliseconds",
                "store the period number in an int field, or use day(now) * 1d for a UTC midnight time (hour(now) * 1h for an hour)"));
        }
        match &field.value {
            Some(value) if expected.required().is_identity() => self.expr_as_reference(value, out, expected),
            Some(value) => {
                let (e, t) = self.expr(value, out)?;
                // A text literal in an enum position is that variant.
                if let (Ty::Enum(variants), Expr::Literal(Value::String(text))) = (expected.required(), &e) {
                    if variants.contains(text) {
                        return Ok((e, Ty::Enum(variants)));
                    }
                    return Err(type_error(value.site(), format!("'{text}' is not one of {}", variants.iter().map(|v| format!("'{v}'")).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")), format!("'{}'", variants.first().cloned().unwrap_or_default())));
                }
                Ok((e, t))
            }
            None => {
                let (value, ty) = self.name(&field.name, &field.site)?;
                Ok(self.row_identity(value, ty, expected))
            },
        }
    }

//! Literal column defaults, shared by schema binding and an insert's returned image.
use super::catalog::TableInfo;
use crate::ast::{ColumnDecl, Expr, Literal, TypeKind};
use crate::diag::{Diagnostic, Fallible, type_error};
use snapback4_core::schema::ColumnDefault;
use snapback4_core::value::Value;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

pub(super) fn bind(info: &TableInfo, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) -> BTreeMap<String, ColumnDefault> {
    let mut defaults = BTreeMap::new();
    for decl in &info.decl.columns {
        if let Some(expr) = &decl.default {
            match column(decl, expr) {
                Ok(default) => { defaults.insert(decl.name.clone(), default); }
                Err(diagnostic) => diagnostics.push(diagnostic),
            }
        }
    }
    defaults
}

pub(super) fn column(decl: &ColumnDecl, expr: &Expr) -> Fallible<ColumnDefault> {
    let bad = || type_error(expr.site(), format!("default for {} must be a literal, now or viewer fitting {}", decl.name, crate::print::scalar_type(&decl.type_)), format!("{}: {} default <literal | now | viewer>", decl.name, crate::print::scalar_type(&decl.type_)));
    let default = match expr {
        Expr::Name { name, .. } if name == "now" && matches!(decl.type_.kind, TypeKind::Time) => ColumnDefault::Now,
        Expr::Name { name, .. } if name == "viewer" && matches!(decl.type_.kind, TypeKind::Principal) => ColumnDefault::Viewer,
        Expr::Literal { value, site } => ColumnDefault::Literal(match value {
            Literal::Str(text) if matches!(decl.type_.kind, TypeKind::Id | TypeKind::Ref { .. } | TypeKind::Principal) => Value::Id(text.clone()),
            Literal::Str(text) => Value::String(text.clone()),
            Literal::Number(text) => Value::Int(super::integer_literal(text, site)?),
            Literal::Bool(b) => Value::Bool(*b),
            Literal::Null => Value::Null,
        }),
        Expr::Unary { op, value, site } if op == "-" => match value.as_ref() {
            Expr::Literal { value: Literal::Number(text), .. } => ColumnDefault::Literal(Value::Int(super::integer_literal(&format!("-{text}"), site)?)),
            _ => return Err(bad()),
        },
        _ => return Err(bad()),
    };
    let value = default.value(0, "dev:default");
    snapback4_core::engine::validate::validate_column("default", &decl.name, &crate::types::scalar_to_column(&decl.type_), Some(&value)).map_err(|_| bad())?;
    if let (TypeKind::Text { min, format, .. }, Value::String(text)) = (&decl.type_.kind, &value) {
        let format = match format.as_deref() {
            Some("handle") => Some(snapback4_core::schema::TextFormat::Handle),
            Some("url") => Some(snapback4_core::schema::TextFormat::Url),
            Some("email") => Some(snapback4_core::schema::TextFormat::Email),
            _ => None,
        };
        snapback4_core::engine::validate::validate_text(&decl.name, text, min.unwrap_or(0), format).map_err(|_| bad())?;
    }
    Ok(default)
}

   113	        return Err(io::Error::other(
   114	            "release control must be a same-owner 0600 socket, never a symlink or regular file",
   115	        ));
   116	    }
   117	    Ok(m)
   118	}
   119	
   120	// @ref LLP 3000.000.000#51-path-independent-control-address — fixed short runtime root, independent of shell environment.
   121	#[cfg(unix)]
   122	fn private_directory(path: &Path, create: bool) -> io::Result<()> {
   123	    if create {
   124	        match fs::DirBuilder::new().mode(0o700).create(path) {
   125	            Ok(()) => {}
   126	            Err(e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::AlreadyExists => {}
   127	            Err(e) => return Err(e),
   128	        }
   129	    }
   130	    // Do not chmod or follow an existing entry. A stranger can pre-create a
   131	    // name in /tmp, but cannot turn that into a capability or chmod target.
   132	    let directory = fs::OpenOptions::new()
   133	        .read(true)
   134	        .custom_flags(libc::O_DIRECTORY | libc::O_NOFOLLOW)
   135	        .open(path)?;
   136	    directory_metadata(&directory.metadata()?, unsafe { libc::geteuid() })
   137	}
   138	
   139	#[cfg(unix)]
   140	fn directory_metadata(m: &fs::Metadata, uid: u32) -> io::Result<()> {
   141	    if !m.is_dir() || m.uid() != uid || m.permissions().mode() & 0o7777 != 0o700 {
   142	        return Err(io::Error::other(
   143	            "release control runtime directory must be a same-owner 0700 directory",
   144	        ));
   145	    }
   146	    Ok(())
   147	}
   148	
   149	#[cfg(unix)]
   150	fn address(dir: &Path, create: bool) -> io::Result<PathBuf> {
   151	    let directory = PathBuf::from(format!("/tmp/snapback4-{}", unsafe { libc::geteuid() }));
   152	    private_directory(&directory, create)?;
   153	    let canonical = dir.canonicalize()?;
   154	    // Bind the address to immutable deployment source, even when two
   155	    // deployments symlink their database to the same store. The actual
   156	    // database path/inode is separately checked in every envelope.
   157	    Ok(directory.join(format!(
   158	        "{}.sock",
   159	        crate::native::digest(canonical.as_os_str().as_bytes())
   160	    )))
   161	}
   162	
   163	// @ref LLP 3000.000.000#51-path-independent-control-address — a total input deadline bounds shutdown even when a peer keeps sending bytes.
   164	#[cfg(unix)]
   165	fn input(stream: &mut UnixStream, timeout: Duration) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>> {
   166	    let deadline = Instant::now() + timeout;
   167	    let mut bytes = Vec::new();
   168	    let mut buffer = [0; INPUT + 1];
   169	    while bytes.len() <= INPUT {
   170	        let remaining = deadline.saturating_duration_since(Instant::now());
   171	        if remaining.is_zero() {
   172	            return Err(io::Error::new(
   173	                io::ErrorKind::TimedOut,
   174	                "release control input deadline exceeded",
   175	            ));
   176	        }
   177	        stream.set_read_timeout(Some(remaining))?;
   178	        match stream.read(&mut buffer[..INPUT + 1 - bytes.len()]) {
   179	            Ok(0) => break,
   180	            Ok(n) => bytes.extend_from_slice(&buffer[..n]),
   181	            Err(e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::Interrupted => continue,
   182	            Err(e) => return Err(e),
   183	        }
   184	    }
   185	    Ok(bytes)
   186	}
   187	
   188	/// Only called while the exclusive database sidecar is held, so stale socket
   189	/// replacement cannot disconnect another admitted serving owner.
   190	#[cfg(unix)]
   191	pub(crate) struct Listener {
   192	    listener: UnixListener,
   193	    path: PathBuf,
   194	    inode: (u64, u64),
   195	    identity: String,
   196	}
   197	#[cfg(unix)]
   198	impl Listener {
   199	    pub(crate) fn bind(dir: &Path, store: &Path) -> Result<Self, String> {
   200	        let identity = identity(store)?;
   201	        let path = address(dir, true).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
   202	        match fs::symlink_metadata(&path) {
   203	            Ok(_) => {
   204	                socket_entry(&path).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
   205	                match UnixStream::connect(&path) {
   206	                    Ok(_) => {
   207	                        return Err("release control socket already has a live listener".into());
   208	                    }
   209	                    Err(e)
   210	                        if matches!(
   211	                            e.kind(),
   212	                            io::ErrorKind::ConnectionRefused | io::ErrorKind::NotFound
   213	                        ) => {}
   214	                    Err(e) => return Err(e.to_string()),
   215	                }
   216	                fs::remove_file(&path).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
   217	            }
   218	            Err(e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {}
   219	            Err(e) => return Err(e.to_string()),
   220	        }
   221	        let listener = UnixListener::bind(&path)
   222	            .map_err(|e| format!("release control {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
   223	        let m = fs::symlink_metadata(&path).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
   224	        let owned = Self {
   225	            listener,
   226	            path,
   227	            inode: (m.dev(), m.ino()),
   228	            identity,
   229	        };
   230	        // Establish cleanup custody before any fallible setup after bind.
   231	        fs::set_permissions(&owned.path, fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o600))
   232	            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
   233	        owned
   234	            .listener
   235	            .set_nonblocking(true)
   236	            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
   237	        socket_entry(&owned.path).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
   238	        Ok(owned)
   239	    }
   240	    fn accept(&self) -> io::Result<UnixStream> {
   241	        let (stream, _) = self.listener.accept()?;
   242	        // Darwin inherits O_NONBLOCK from the listener; input's deadline and
   243	        // socket timeouts require blocking I/O, even before the client writes.
   244	        stream.set_nonblocking(false)?;
   245	        Ok(stream)
   246	    }
   247	    fn handle(
   248	        &self,
   249	        stream: &mut UnixStream,
   250	        mut handle: impl FnMut(Command) -> Result<Value, String>,
   251	    ) {
   252	        let result = (|| -> Result<Value, String> {
   253	            peer(&stream).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
   254	            stream
   255	                .set_write_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(5)))
   256	                .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
   257	            let bytes = input(stream, Duration::from_secs(5)).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
   258	            if bytes.len() > INPUT {
   259	                return Err("release control command exceeds 4096 bytes".into());
   260	            }
   261	            let request: Envelope = serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
   262	            if request.identity != self.identity {
   263	                return Err("release control store identity differs; run releases against the owned deployment".into());
   264	            }
   265	            handle(request.command)
   266	        })();
   267	        let reply = match result {
   268	            Ok(value) => json!({"ok":value}),
   269	            Err(error) => json!({"error":error}),
   270	        };
   271	        let mut bytes = serde_json::to_vec(&reply).unwrap();
   272	        if bytes.len() > OUTPUT {
   273	            bytes=serde_json::to_vec(&json!({"error":"release control reply exceeds its bound; inspect paginated `snapback4 releases <dir>`; an admitted activation/prune may already have committed"})).unwrap();
   274	        }
   275	        // A timeout/lost peer does not cancel or undo admitted work.
   276	        let _ = stream.write_all(&bytes);
   277	    }
   278	    pub(crate) fn run(self, mut handle: impl FnMut(Command) -> Result<Value, String>) {
   279	        while !crate::lifecycle::stopping() {
   280	            match self.accept() {
   281	                Ok(mut stream) => {
   282	                    self.handle(&mut stream, &mut handle);
   283	                }
   284	                Err(e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock => {
   285	                    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(25))
   286	                }
   287	                Err(e) => {
   288	                    snapback4_core::diagnostic!("release control accept: {e}");
   289	                    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50));
   290	                }
   291	            }
   292	        }
   293	    }
   294	}
   295	#[cfg(unix)]
   296	impl Drop for Listener {
   297	    fn drop(&mut self) {
   298	        if fs::symlink_metadata(&self.path)
   299	            .is_ok_and(|m| m.file_type().is_socket() && (m.dev(), m.ino()) == self.inode)
   300	        {
   301	            let _ = fs::remove_file(&self.path);
   302	        }
   303	    }
   304	}
   305	
   306	#[cfg(unix)]
   307	pub(crate) fn request(dir: &Path, command: Command) -> Result<Value, String> {
   308	    let store = dir.join("store.sqlite");
   309	    let unavailable = |reason: String| {
   310	        let owner_path = store.canonicalize().unwrap_or_else(|_| store.clone());
   311	        let detail = if reason.contains("No such file or directory") {
   312	            "this deployment has no release control socket".to_owned()
   313	        } else {
   314	            reason
   315	        };
   316	        format!(
   317	            "{}; release control unavailable: {detail}; stop `snapback4 serve {}`, rerun the exact command, then `snapback4 serve {}`",
   318	            crate::store_owner::busy(&owner_path),
   319	            dir.display(),
   320	            dir.display()
   321	        )
   322	    };
   323	    let path = address(dir, false).map_err(|e| unavailable(e.to_string()))?;
   324	    let before = socket_entry(&path).map_err(|e| unavailable(e.to_string()))?;
   325	    let mut stream = UnixStream::connect(&path).map_err(|e| unavailable(e.to_string()))?;
   326	    peer(&stream).map_err(|e| unavailable(e.to_string()))?;
   327	    let after = socket_entry(&path).map_err(|e| unavailable(e.to_string()))?;
   328	    if (before.dev(), before.ino()) != (after.dev(), after.ino()) {
   329	        return Err(unavailable(
   330	            "release control socket changed before send".into(),
   331	        ));
   332	    }
   333	    stream
   334	        .set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(120)))
   335	        .map_err(|e| unavailable(e.to_string()))?;
   336	    stream
   337	        .set_write_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(5)))
   338	        .map_err(|e| unavailable(e.to_string()))?;
   339	    let bytes = serde_json::to_vec(&Envelope {
   340	        identity: identity(&store)?,
   341	        command,
   342	    })
   343	    .unwrap();
   344	    if bytes.len() > INPUT {
   345	        return Err("release control command exceeds 4096 bytes".into());
   346	    }
   347	    let ambiguous = |reason: io::Error| {
   348	        format!(
   349	            "release command result is unknown: {reason}; run `snapback4 releases {}` to inspect database authority; the server continues admitted work. Do not automatically deploy another release",
   350	            dir.display()
   351	        )
   352	    };
   353	    stream.write_all(&bytes).map_err(ambiguous)?;
   354	    stream
   355	        .shutdown(std::net::Shutdown::Write)
   356	        .map_err(ambiguous)?;
   357	    let mut reply = Vec::new();
   358	    stream
   359	        .take((OUTPUT + 1) as u64)
   360	        .read_to_end(&mut reply)
   361	        .map_err(ambiguous)?;
   362	    if reply.len() > OUTPUT {
   363	        return Err("release reply too large; inspect releases before retrying".into());
   364	    }
   365	    let value: Value = serde_json::from_slice(&reply).map_err(|e| {
   366	        format!(
   367	            "release result is unknown ({e}); inspect `snapback4 releases {}` before retrying",
   368	            dir.display()
   369	        )
   370	    })?;
   371	    match value.get("ok") {
   372	        Some(value) => Ok(value.clone()),
   373	        None => Err(value["error"]
   374	            .as_str()
   375	            .unwrap_or("release control refused command; inspect releases")
   376	            .into()),
   377	    }
   378	}
   379	
   380	#[cfg(not(unix))]
   381	pub(crate) fn request(_: &Path, _: Command) -> Result<Value, String> {
   382	    Err("local release control requires Unix".into())
   383	}

   385	#[cfg(all(test, unix))]
   386	mod tests {
   387	    use super::*;
   388	    use std::sync::{
   389	        atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering},
   390	        mpsc,
   391	    };
   392	    static NEXT: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
   393	    struct Directory(PathBuf);
   394	    impl Directory {
   395	        fn new(long: bool) -> Self {
   396	            let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
   397	                "sb4-roll-control-{}-{}",
   398	                std::process::id(),
   399	                NEXT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)
   400	            ));
   401	            let root = if long {
   402	                root.join("long-path-component".repeat(6))
   403	            } else {
   404	                root
   405	            };
   406	            snapback4_core::private_fs::directory(&root).unwrap();
   407	            let _store = snapback4_core::Store::open(&root.join("store.sqlite")).unwrap();
   408	            Self(root)
   409	        }
   410	    }
   411	    impl Drop for Directory {
   412	        fn drop(&mut self) {
   413	            let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0);
   414	        }
   415	    }
   416	    #[test]
   417	    fn socket_permissions_and_entry_types_are_enforced() {
   418	        let dir = Directory::new(false);
   419	        let path = address(&dir.0, true).unwrap();
   420	        fs::write(&path, "not a socket").unwrap();
   421	        assert!(
   422	            Listener::bind(&dir.0, &dir.0.join("store.sqlite"))
   423	                .err()
   424	                .unwrap()
   425	                .contains("0600 socket")
   426	        );
   427	        fs::remove_file(&path).unwrap();
   428	        std::os::unix::fs::symlink("store.sqlite", &path).unwrap();
   429	        assert!(Listener::bind(&dir.0, &dir.0.join("store.sqlite")).is_err());
   430	        fs::remove_file(&path).unwrap();
   431	        let listener = Listener::bind(&dir.0, &dir.0.join("store.sqlite")).unwrap();
   432	        assert_eq!(
   433	            fs::metadata(&path).unwrap().permissions().mode() & 0o777,
   434	            0o600
   435	        );
   436	        for mode in [0o666, 0o1600] {
   437	            fs::set_permissions(&path, fs::Permissions::from_mode(mode)).unwrap();
   438	            assert!(
   439	                request(
   440	                    &dir.0,
   441	                    Command::Status {
   442	                        after: 0,
   443	                        items_after: None,
   444	                        event: None
   445	                    }
   446	                )
   447	                .unwrap_err()
   448	                .contains("0600 socket")
   449	            );
   450	        }
   451	        drop(listener);
   452	        assert!(!path.exists());
   453	    }
   454	    #[test]
   455	    fn accepted_nonblocking_listener_waits_for_delayed_client_input() {
   456	        let dir = Directory::new(false);
   457	        let listener = Listener::bind(&dir.0, &dir.0.join("store.sqlite")).unwrap();
   458	        let path = listener.path.clone();
   459	        let envelope = Envelope {
   460	            identity: listener.identity.clone(),
   461	            command: Command::Status { after: 0, items_after: None, event: None },
   462	        };
   463	        // Connect before starting accept so the listener stays nonblocking.
   464	        let mut client = UnixStream::connect(&path).unwrap();
   465	        client.set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(10))).unwrap();
   466	        client.set_write_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(10))).unwrap();
   467	        let (accepted, waiting) = mpsc::channel();
   468	        let task = std::thread::spawn(move || {
   469	            let mut stream = listener.accept().unwrap();
   470	            accepted.send(()).unwrap();
   471	            listener.handle(&mut stream, |command| {
   472	                assert!(matches!(command, Command::Status { after: 0, .. }));
   473	                Ok(json!({"delayed":true}))
   474	            });
   475	        });
   476	        waiting.recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(10)).unwrap();
   477	        // Without normalization Darwin reads WouldBlock and closes the peer
   478	        // here. Linux accept does not inherit O_NONBLOCK, so it cannot expose
   479	        // the unfixed platform bug with this test.
   480	        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));
   481	        client.write_all(&serde_json::to_vec(&envelope).unwrap()).unwrap();
   482	        client.shutdown(std::net::Shutdown::Write).unwrap();
   483	        let mut reply = String::new();
   484	        client.read_to_string(&mut reply).unwrap();
   485	        task.join().unwrap();
   486	        assert_eq!(serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&reply).unwrap(), json!({"ok":{"delayed":true}}));
   487	    }
   488	    #[test]
   489	    fn input_deadline_expires_while_the_peer_keeps_sending() {
   490	        let (mut reader, mut writer) = UnixStream::pair().unwrap();
   491	        let task = std::thread::spawn(move || {
   492	            while writer.write_all(b" ").is_ok() {
   493	                std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20));
   494	            }
   495	        });
   496	        let started = Instant::now();
   497	        let error = input(&mut reader, Duration::from_millis(300)).unwrap_err();
   498	        assert!(
   499	            matches!(
   500	                error.kind(),
   501	                io::ErrorKind::TimedOut | io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock
   502	            ),
   503	            "{error}"
   504	        );
   505	        assert!(
   506	            started.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(2),
   507	            "input deadline reset on each read"
   508	        );
   509	        drop(reader);
   510	        task.join().unwrap();
   511	    }

   594	    #[test]
   595	    fn lost_reply_does_not_cancel_admitted_command() {
   596	        let dir = Directory::new(false);
   597	        let listener = Listener::bind(&dir.0, &dir.0.join("store.sqlite")).unwrap();
   598	        listener.listener.set_nonblocking(false).unwrap();
   599	        let (entered, waiting) = mpsc::channel();
   600	        let (resume, resumed) = mpsc::channel();
   601	        let (done, finished) = mpsc::channel();
   602	        let task = std::thread::spawn(move || {
   603	            let (mut stream, _) = listener.listener.accept().unwrap();
   604	            listener.handle(&mut stream, |_| {
   605	                entered.send(()).unwrap();
   606	                resumed.recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(10)).unwrap();
   607	                done.send(()).unwrap();
   608	                Ok(json!({"committed":true}))
   609	            });
   610	        });
   611	        let mut stream = UnixStream::connect(address(&dir.0, true).unwrap()).unwrap();
   612	        let envelope = Envelope {
   613	            identity: identity(&dir.0.join("store.sqlite")).unwrap(),
   614	            command: Command::Prune {
   615	                confirm: true,
   616	                expected_revision: 1,
   617	            },
   618	        };
   619	        stream
   620	            .write_all(&serde_json::to_vec(&envelope).unwrap())

# TypeScript server handlers

One `use server` in any module (`schema.q` is usual) enables the whole
project; repeating it is harmless. Actions, routes and schedules naming an
action require it. Effects (including secrets, retry, backoff, deadline and
cancellation), jobs, schedules naming a job and service seats need no directive.

## Release lifecycle

`deploy <dir>` stages immutable source, validates the live data and selects a release.
`rollback <dir>` selects the previously active release from committed history; `rollback <dir> --to N`
selects any successfully adopted release, including a deliberate roll forward (`--to latest` selects the highest successfully adopted
source). `releases` exposes `release`, `latest` and `generation` separately. Both activate
inside a running `serve` process without restarting it. A stopped deployment uses
the same transaction offline. They return after the runtime switches and print
`release N is current as generation G`. Identical packaged source is a no-op.
Default adoption output is one measured receipt; --verbose/--json includes phases.

`deploy <dir> --check`, `rollback <dir> --to N --check` and `check --store <dir>/store.sqlite --release N`
run exact adoption on a private, disk-backed snapshot without activating. They
report dormant populations and any E_ADOPT constraint/backfill refusal. The snapshot
can require storage/time proportional to the database; later writes can change the
plan. Compatibility warnings include the existing row count and appear only for
populated tables. Deploy warns on widening; rollback warns when the target admits values the
current source refuses. See guide deploy's rollback-after-widening recipe and its
business-compatibility checklist: old code cannot enforce logic it never contained.

Refused candidates stay unselectable, including by an explicit numeric selector.
A pending source directory becomes selectable only when database activation history
proves its adoption committed, including after a lost reply or pointer-copy failure.
The release receipt includes sample dormant ids; preview also flags removed schedules
and populated tables whose holds or other safeguards the selected release lacks.
Full service seats can trigger system jobs with `run <job> --release <dir>` and
`SNAPBACK4_SERVICE_TOKEN` (or `--token-env NAME`); see guide deploy's recipe.

### Retained storage and roll forward

Removed durable tables, columns and index definitions become **dormant**. They
stay in separate private storage, invisible to the older programs, rules, sync and
clients. Forward activation restores their data and rebuilds indexes against the
current rows. Rollback selects source; it does not rewind application writes.

- Updating a row under the older release preserves its dormant column values.
- Deleting an active row removes its dormant values. Reusing its id cannot
  resurrect those values. Deleting a parent invalidates dormant references to
  its lifetime, including when an identical parent id/value is recreated.
- Referential actions come from the active schema only. A newer cascade or
  restrict on a dormant table/column is inactive after rollback. Deleting its
  active parent invalidates the retained edge; forward restoration refuses
  `E_ADOPT` even after identical id reuse. If the reference stays active, its
  selected release's action applies (including the default restrict).
- A new row written under the older release receives the forward schema's literal
  default or optional null when its newer field is reactivated. Existing dormant
  values restore verbatim, including the defaults they previously represented.
- A required column without a literal default refuses when older-release rows
  lack it. Deploy a bridge with that field optional or defaulted using
  `--restore-dormant`, backfill through a bridge mutation, then deploy the required
  definition. `default now` and `default viewer` never invent historical values.
- An enum/text/type value that cannot inhabit the selected release makes its
  whole row dormant. Full original values restore on a compatible release. This
  also handles a short code written by a looser old release on roll-forward.
  Missing newly required fields still need backfill; no value is silently coerced.
- Rows referencing those dormant rows become dormant too, including nested/list
  references and authorization memberships. Counts, maintained views, cap occupancy,
  indexes, application SQL and sync use only the active population. Changed
  generations reacquire that population, with no retained dormant device authority.
- Dormant ids stay reserved. Point lookups/updates/deletes see absent rows; inserts
  cannot overwrite them (E_RULE, like a hidden live conflict). Nominal references
  remain legal, as they are for nonexistent ids; require/read-through rules decide
  live-target admission. New such references never grant dormant authority. Their other unique keys/caps do not reserve active slots.
  An old write may therefore need duplicate repair before forward restoration.
- Actual parent deletion invalidates dormant narrowed references. Those rows stay
  dormant on forward rather than rebinding a reused parent id. Existing whole-table
  or column restoration still refuses its invalid lifetime. Read-through capture
  validation continues to protect the original audience/deadline.
- Engine captures retire into dormant columns with their source definition. Restoring
  the same read-through definition uses the original captures, not the widened
  release audience. Deleted parent lifetimes and changed captures still refuse.
- A newly introduced unique index can refuse forward if older writes created
  duplicate keys. Restored references also refuse deleted/reused parents or changed
  read-through audience captures. Authoritative storage cannot become derived
  storage implicitly. Refusals preserve the current release and dormant data.

Reusing dormant names in **new source** requires `deploy <dir> --restore-dormant`.
Selecting an immutable release with `rollback --to N` explicitly selects restoration.
A partial table restoration preserves omitted newer columns as dormant; another
forward can recover them. A rename has two independent names.

`prune <dir>` previews dormant tables, columns and indexes, row counts, logical
serialized bytes, retained asset bytes and sample ids. `prune <dir> --allow-destructive`
permanently removes **all** currently dormant storage and records the exact set in
history. Active rows/programs stay active; later restoration gets empty tables and
ordinary default/backfill behavior. There is no automatic age/size pruning.
`--allow-destructive` on deploy/rollback does not prune or bypass validation.
To convert durable to ephemeral, first deploy without that table, explicitly

#[cfg(unix)]
pub(crate) fn request(dir: &Path, command: Command) -> Result<Value, String> {
    let store = dir.join("store.sqlite");
    let unavailable = |reason: String| {
        let owner_path = store.canonicalize().unwrap_or_else(|_| store.clone());
        let detail = if reason.contains("No such file or directory") {
            "this deployment has no release control socket".to_owned()
        } else {
            reason
        };
        format!(
            "{}; release control unavailable: {detail}; stop `snapback4 serve {}`, rerun the exact command, then `snapback4 serve {}`",
            crate::store_owner::busy(&owner_path),
            dir.display(),
            dir.display()
        )
    };
    let path = address(dir, false).map_err(|e| unavailable(e.to_string()))?;
    let before = socket_entry(&path).map_err(|e| unavailable(e.to_string()))?;
    let mut stream = UnixStream::connect(&path).map_err(|e| unavailable(e.to_string()))?;
    peer(&stream).map_err(|e| unavailable(e.to_string()))?;
    let after = socket_entry(&path).map_err(|e| unavailable(e.to_string()))?;
    if (before.dev(), before.ino()) != (after.dev(), after.ino()) {
        return Err(unavailable(
            "release control socket changed before send".into(),
        ));
    }
    stream
        .set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(120)))
        .map_err(|e| unavailable(e.to_string()))?;
    stream
        .set_write_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(5)))
        .map_err(|e| unavailable(e.to_string()))?;
    let bytes = serde_json::to_vec(&Envelope {
        identity: identity(&store)?,
        command,
    })
    .unwrap();
    if bytes.len() > INPUT {
        return Err("release control command exceeds 4096 bytes".into());
    }
    let ambiguous = |reason: io::Error| {
        format!(
            "release command result is unknown: {reason}; run `snapback4 releases {}` to inspect database authority; the server continues admitted work. Do not automatically deploy another release",
            dir.display()
        )
    };
    stream.write_all(&bytes).map_err(ambiguous)?;
    stream
        .shutdown(std::net::Shutdown::Write)

codex
The cleanup path can delete source for an activation that is still able to commit after the client times out. I also confirmed a reporting gap: widening a stored integer from `0..10` to `0..20` produces no compatibility warning when a query returns that field in an object. The cached language tests passed; I haven’t run broader or packed qualification.

codex
Reviewed revision `b5d5a1c4e27ed44012fd80e188c4d99e84e3eaac` against `sb4-loop`. Two material concerns remain.

1. **P1 — Ambiguous activation cleanup can delete source that subsequently commits.**  
   [release_files.rs:191](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-b17-rel5/snapback4/crates/snapback4/src/release_files.rs:191)

   `Candidate::drop()` deletes the numeric directory whenever its history query finds no committed activation. That does not establish a terminal non-commit: the control request times out after 120 seconds while the server continues admitted work. An activation waiting for the engine lock, or still inside its adoption transaction, remains invisible to the WAL reader. Cleanup can therefore remove its source before the server commits and selects that release. The running backend may finish switching, but restart and recovery then lack the selected immutable source.

   Preserve candidates after transport ambiguity regardless of an immediate negative history query. Delete only after a definitive refusal or reconciliation that excludes further activation. Add a regression holding activation before commit, losing the reply, then completing activation and verifying source retention and restart.

2. **P2 — Compatibility reporting misses changed domains in projected results.**  
   [client_contracts.rs:30](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-b17-rel5/snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/src/client_contracts.rs:30)

   Result comparison relies on `Ty`, which erases integer ranges, and explicitly normalizes text bounds to `"string"`. Consequently, widening a stored field from `int 0..10` to `int 0..20` produces no `RESULT REVIEW` when the unchanged query returns `{n: row.n}`. Old callers can receive newly admitted values without the commissioned result-domain warning. Returning the whole nominal row does detect the same change, making reporting inconsistent across projections.

   I confirmed that both schemas compile and `compare()` returns `[]` for this case. Preserve declared domain provenance for projected fields, or conservatively report changes to their source domains. Cover projected integer and text bounds alongside nominal-row comparisons.

Validation was bounded: two existing cached operation-evolution binaries each passed four tests, and temporary compiler probes confirmed the result-reporting gap and inspected default lowering. Those binaries did not contain the newly added device-roundtrip test. I did not rebuild, run broad suites, or execute packed qualification. No repository files were modified.

VERDICT: NOT READY
